questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to sort the result set?
What is the purpose of the WHERE clause in a SELECT statement?
choices: To specify the columns to be selected
To filter rows based on a condition
To group rows based on a common column
questions.correct_answer: To filter rows based on a condition

questions.question_text: Which of the following queries is more efficient given that there is an index on LastName?
choices: SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE LastName = 'Smith';
SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE UPPER(LastName) = 'SMITH';
questions.correct_answer: SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE LastName = 'Smith';
questions.explanation: Using a function like UPPER on an indexed column negates the benefit of the index, making the query less efficient.

questions.question_text:
Complete the following query to calculate the total sales for each product category:
SELECT p.Category, SUM(s.Amount) AS TotalSales
FROM Sales s
JOIN Products p ON s.ProductID = p.ProductID
GROUP BY ___________;
questions.explanation: GROUP BY is used to aggregate results by a specific column. In this case, we're aggregating by Category.

questions.question_text: What does the DISTINCT keyword do?
choices: It removes duplicate rows from the result set.
It sorts the result set in ascending order.
It groups rows by a common column.
It filters rows based on a condition.
questions.correct_answer: It removes duplicate rows from the result set.

questions.question_text: Which function is used to calculate the total sum of a numeric column?
Which SQL statement is used to fetch the first 10 rows from a table named Employees?
choices: SELECT * FROM Employees FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS;

questions.question_text: What does the COUNT() function do?
choices: It returns the number of rows that match a specified criterion.
It calculates the sum of a numeric column.
It groups rows by a common column.
questions.correct_answer: It returns the number of rows that match a specified criterion.

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to restrict the groups returned by the GROUP BY clause?
Which of the following is the correct syntax to rename a column in a result set?
choices: SELECT FirstName AS Name FROM Employees;
SELECT FirstName RENAME TO Name FROM Employees;
SELECT Name AS FirstName FROM Employees;
SELECT FirstName TO Name FROM Employees;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT FirstName AS Name FROM Employees;

questions.question_text: Which SQL function returns the average value of a numeric column?
Which SQL clause is used to filter rows returned by a query?
What is the correct SQL statement to select all the columns from a table named Customers?
Which SQL clause is used to eliminate duplicate rows in a result set?
Which of the following queries is more efficient for retrieving specific columns from a table?
choices: SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE EmployeeID = 101;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName FROM Employees WHERE EmployeeID = 101;
questions.explanation: Selecting specific columns rather than all columns (*) is generally more efficient, especially in tables with many columns.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is more efficient for counting the number of rows in a large table?
choices: SELECT TOP 1 * FROM TableName ORDER BY ColumnName;
SELECT COUNT(ColumnName) FROM TableName WHERE ColumnName IS NOT NULL;
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) is the most efficient way to count rows, as it is optimized to quickly return the total row count.

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to group rows that have the same values in specified columns into summary rows?
What is the primary purpose of the SQL WHERE clause?
choices: To filter records based on a specified condition.
questions.correct_answer: To filter records based on a specified condition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL statements is used to insert a new record into a table?
Which SQL keyword is used to retrieve only unique values from a column?
Which SQL function returns the maximum value in a set of values?
Which SQL function returns the minimum value in a set of values?
What is the purpose of the SQL HAVING clause?
choices: To filter groups based on a condition.
To filter rows based on a condition.
questions.correct_answer: To filter groups based on a condition.

questions.question_text: Which SQL statement is used to modify existing records in a table?
Which SQL keyword is used to retrieve all columns from a table?
Which SQL clause is used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column?
Which SQL function is used to calculate the average of a numeric column?
Which SQL statement is used to remove records from a table?
Which SQL keyword is used to retrieve all columns from a table?
Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table and the matched rows from the right table?
Which of the following queries would be more efficient for retrieving all orders along with the customer names, assuming there are indexes on CustomerID in both tables?
choices: SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerName FROM Orders o INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID;
SELECT o.OrderID, (SELECT CustomerName FROM Customers c WHERE c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID) FROM Orders o;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerName FROM Orders o INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID;
questions.explanation: Joins are generally more efficient than subqueries in the SELECT clause, especially when indexes are involved.

questions.question_text: In SQL, what is a correlated subquery?
choices: A subquery that depends on the outer query for its values
A subquery that is independent of the outer query
A subquery that joins two tables
A subquery that returns multiple rows
questions.correct_answer: A subquery that depends on the outer query for its values

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column?
Which SQL keyword is used to specify a condition while combining rows from two tables?
Which type of JOIN returns only the rows that have matching values in both tables?
Which SQL keyword is used to combine the results of two queries into a single result set?
Which of the following is an example of a correlated subquery?
choices: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE EmployeeID = (SELECT MAX(EmployeeID) FROM Employees);
SELECT * FROM Employees e WHERE e.Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE EmployeeID IN (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Orders);
SELECT EmployeeName FROM Employees WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders WHERE Orders.EmployeeID = Employees.EmployeeID);
questions.correct_answer: SELECT * FROM Employees e WHERE e.Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID);

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows returned by a query?
What does the RIGHT JOIN do in SQL?
choices: Returns all rows from the right table and the matched rows from the left table
Returns all rows from the left table and the matched rows from the right table
Returns only the rows that have matching values in both tables
Combines the results of two queries into a single result set
questions.correct_answer: Returns all rows from the right table and the matched rows from the left table

questions.question_text: Which of the following is more efficient for filtering data in a JOIN operation?
choices: Applying the condition in the WHERE clause after the JOIN
Applying the condition in the ON clause during the JOIN
questions.correct_answer: Applying the condition in the ON clause during the JOIN
questions.explanation: Applying the condition in the ON clause during the JOIN can reduce the amount of data processed and improve efficiency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following queries would be more efficient for retrieving the highest salary in each department?
choices: SELECT DepartmentID, MAX(Salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY DepartmentID;
SELECT e.DepartmentID, e.Salary FROM Employees e WHERE e.Salary = (SELECT MAX(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID);
questions.correct_answer: SELECT DepartmentID, MAX(Salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY DepartmentID;
questions.explanation: Using GROUP BY with an aggregate function is typically more efficient than using a correlated subquery.

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to restrict the groups returned by the GROUP BY clause?
Which of the following scenarios is best suited for using a correlated subquery?
choices: When you need to reference a column from the outer query within the subquery
When you need to combine rows from two tables
When you need to filter rows based on a condition
When you need to group rows by a common column
questions.correct_answer: When you need to reference a column from the outer query within the subquery

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to ensure that only matching rows from both tables are included in the result set?
Which of the following SQL queries uses a correlated subquery?
choices: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employees);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID IN (SELECT DepartmentID FROM Departments);
SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employees);
questions.correct_answer: SELECT e.FirstName, e.LastName FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID);

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the SQL ON clause in a JOIN operation?
choices: To specify the condition for joining rows from two tables
To filter rows based on a condition
To group rows by a common column
questions.correct_answer: To specify the condition for joining rows from two tables

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to return all rows from two tables, regardless of whether there is a match?
Which of the following SQL queries uses a JOIN operation?
choices: SELECT * FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID;
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employees);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID IN (SELECT DepartmentID FROM Departments);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders);
questions.correct_answer: SELECT * FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID;

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows in a subquery?
Which SQL keyword is used to return rows from one table that do not have a match in another table?
Which SQL keyword is used to return rows from the right table that do not have a match in the left table?
Which of the following SQL queries uses a JOIN operation with a WHERE clause?
choices: SELECT * FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID WHERE e.Salary > 50000;
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM Employees);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID IN (SELECT DepartmentID FROM Departments);
SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders);
questions.correct_answer: SELECT * FROM Employees e JOIN Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID WHERE e.Salary > 50000;

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column?
Which SQL keyword is used to return all rows from the left table and only the matched rows from the right table?
Which of the following is a common use case for a correlated subquery?
choices: Filtering rows based on a condition that depends on the outer query
Combining rows from two or more tables
Grouping rows by a common column
questions.correct_answer: Filtering rows based on a condition that depends on the outer query

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to specify a condition for joining rows from two tables?
Which SQL keyword is used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column?
Which SQL keyword is used to return all rows from two tables, regardless of whether there is a match?
What is a window function in SQL?
choices: A function that operates on a set of rows and returns a single aggregated value for each row
A function that operates on a set of rows and returns multiple aggregated values for each row
A function that partitions the result set into groups
A function that joins multiple tables together
questions.correct_answer: A function that operates on a set of rows and returns a single aggregated value for each row

questions.question_text: What does the RANK() function do in SQL Server?
choices: Assigns a unique sequential integer to rows within a partition of a result set
Returns the rank of each row within the partition of a result set
Partitions the result set into equal groups
Returns the row number for each row within a partition of a result set
questions.correct_answer: Returns the rank of each row within the partition of a result set

questions.question_text: Which of the following queries would be more efficient for calculating the cumulative sum of sales in SQL Server?
choices: SELECT SUM(SalesAmount) OVER (ORDER BY SalesDate) AS CumulativeSales FROM Sales;
SELECT SalesDate, SUM(SalesAmount) FROM Sales GROUP BY SalesDate ORDER BY SalesDate;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT SUM(SalesAmount) OVER (ORDER BY SalesDate) AS CumulativeSales FROM Sales;
questions.explanation: Using the SUM() OVER() window function is more efficient for calculating cumulative sums without the need for GROUP BY.

questions.question_text: Which function is used to calculate the difference in days between two dates in SQL Server?
What does the PARTITION BY clause do in a window function?
choices: It divides the result set into partitions and performs the window function within each partition
It filters the result set based on a specified condition
It groups the result set by a specified column
questions.correct_answer: It divides the result set into partitions and performs the window function within each partition

questions.question_text: Which SQL function is used to return a value if the expression is NULL?

Complete the following query to rank employees based on their salaries within each department:
SELECT EmployeeName, DepartmentID, Salary,
RANK() OVER (__________) AS SalaryRank
FROM Employees;
choices: PARTITION BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC
GROUP BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC
PARTITION BY Salary ORDER BY DepartmentID
ORDER BY Salary DESC PARTITION BY DepartmentID
questions.correct_answer: PARTITION BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC
questions.explanation: Remember, PARTITION BY is like a GROUP BY within a window function, and ORDER BY determines the ranking.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is more efficient for finding the top 3 salaries in each department?
choices: SELECT TOP 3 Salary FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID = ? ORDER BY Salary DESC;
SELECT Salary FROM (SELECT Salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS Rank FROM Employees) WHERE Rank <= 3;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT Salary FROM (SELECT Salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DepartmentID ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS Rank FROM Employees) WHERE Rank <= 3;
questions.explanation: Using a window function with RANK() is more efficient and flexible for finding the top N records within each group.

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to return the number of rows in a partition of a window function?
What is the purpose of the LEAD() function in SQL Server?
choices: To return the value of the next row in the result set within the same partition
To return the value of the previous row in the result set within the same partition
To calculate the cumulative sum of values within a partition
To return the first value in the result set within the same partition
questions.correct_answer: To return the value of the next row in the result set within the same partition

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the LAG() function in SQL Server?
choices: To return the value of the previous row in the result set within the same partition
To return the value of the next row in the result set within the same partition
To calculate the cumulative sum of values within a partition
To return the last value in the result set within the same partition
questions.correct_answer: To return the value of the previous row in the result set within the same partition

questions.question_text: Which of the following queries would be more efficient for finding gaps in a sequence of IDs?
choices: SELECT ID FROM Table1 WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM Table2);
SELECT ID FROM Table1 EXCEPT SELECT ID FROM Table2;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT ID FROM Table1 EXCEPT SELECT ID FROM Table2;
questions.explanation: Using the EXCEPT clause is generally more efficient for finding differences between two sets.

questions.question_text: What does the ROW_NUMBER() function do in SQL Server?
choices: Assigns a unique sequential integer to rows within a partition of a result set
Returns the rank of each row within the partition of a result set
Partitions the result set into equal groups
Returns the row number for each row within a partition of a result set
questions.correct_answer: Assigns a unique sequential integer to rows within a partition of a result set

questions.question_text: Which of the following is more efficient for calculating running totals?
choices: SELECT SUM(SalesAmount) OVER (ORDER BY SalesDate) AS RunningTotal FROM Sales;
SELECT SalesDate, SUM(SalesAmount) AS RunningTotal FROM Sales GROUP BY SalesDate ORDER BY SalesDate;
questions.correct_answer: SELECT SUM(SalesAmount) OVER (ORDER BY SalesDate) AS RunningTotal FROM Sales;
questions.explanation: Using the SUM() OVER() window function is more efficient for calculating running totals.

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause is used to perform calculations across a set of table rows that are somehow related to the current row?
Which of the following is generally more efficient when filtering large datasets?
choices: Using an index on the filtering column
Using a full table scan without an index
questions.correct_answer: Using an index on the filtering column
questions.explanation: Indexes significantly improve query performance by reducing the number of rows that need to be scanned.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of an execution plan in SQL Server?
choices: To visualize the steps SQL Server takes to execute a query
To format the SQL code for readability
To create a backup of the database
To partition data across multiple servers
questions.correct_answer: To visualize the steps SQL Server takes to execute a query

questions.question_text: Which of the following techniques is more efficient for deleting a large number of rows in a table?
choices: Using DELETE with a WHERE clause
Using a correlated subquery with DELETE
Using DELETE without any WHERE clause
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE TABLE is more efficient for deleting all rows because it deallocates the data pages, rather than logging each row deletion individually.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would typically improve the performance of a query that joins two large tables?
choices: Creating indexes on the join columns
Using a nested subquery instead of a JOIN
Adding an ORDER BY clause to the query
questions.correct_answer: Creating indexes on the join columns
questions.explanation: Indexes on join columns can significantly reduce the amount of data that needs to be processed, speeding up the query.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature helps you analyze and optimize the performance of queries?
What does the term 'query optimization' refer to in SQL Server?
choices: The process of improving the execution speed of SQL queries
The process of formatting SQL code
The process of backing up databases
The process of creating database schemas
questions.correct_answer: The process of improving the execution speed of SQL queries

questions.question_text: Which of the following is more efficient for counting the number of rows in a large table?
choices: SELECT TOP 1 * FROM TableName ORDER BY ColumnName;
SELECT COUNT(ColumnName) FROM TableName WHERE ColumnName IS NOT NULL;
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) is the most efficient way to count rows, as it is optimized to quickly return the total row count.

questions.question_text: Which type of index is generally better for improving performance in a table with frequent read and write operations?
questions.explanation: A clustered index stores data in the table itself and is generally better for performance, especially when rows are frequently read and written.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a method to reduce the impact of locking in SQL Server?
questions.explanation: Row versioning can reduce the impact of locking by allowing readers to access a consistent snapshot of the data without waiting for locks to be released.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a more efficient way to update a large number of rows in a table?
choices: Using an UPDATE statement with a WHERE clause
Using a cursor to update each row individually
Using a DELETE followed by an INSERT
Using an UPDATE statement without any WHERE clause
questions.correct_answer: Using an UPDATE statement with a WHERE clause
questions.explanation: An UPDATE statement with a WHERE clause is generally more efficient because it allows SQL Server to focus only on the rows that need to be updated.

questions.question_text: Which type of query is more likely to benefit from the use of a covering index?
choices: A query that retrieves all columns from a table
A query that retrieves a specific subset of columns frequently
A query that performs a full-text search
A query that uses an aggregate function like SUM()
questions.correct_answer: A query that retrieves a specific subset of columns frequently
questions.explanation: A covering index includes all the columns a query needs, reducing the need to access the actual table and improving performance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common cause of slow query performance in SQL Server?
choices: Missing indexes on frequently queried columns
Having too many indexes on a table
Storing large objects (LOBs) in separate tables
questions.correct_answer: Missing indexes on frequently queried columns

questions.question_text: What is the effect of using the OPTION (RECOMPILE) query hint in SQL Server?
choices: It forces SQL Server to recompile the query each time it is executed, potentially improving performance for parameter-sensitive queries.
It prevents SQL Server from using indexes, leading to a full table scan.
It allows SQL Server to use a cached execution plan, improving performance for repeated executions.
It instructs SQL Server to store the query results in a temporary table.
questions.correct_answer: It forces SQL Server to recompile the query each time it is executed, potentially improving performance for parameter-sensitive queries.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using table partitioning in SQL Server?
choices: Improved query performance by allowing SQL Server to process partitions independently
Decreased performance due to additional overhead
Limited ability to perform parallel queries
questions.correct_answer: Improved query performance by allowing SQL Server to process partitions independently

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to analyze and optimize the performance of queries by providing detailed information about the execution plan?
What is the effect of using a WHERE clause with a non-indexed column in a SQL query?
choices: It can cause a full table scan, potentially slowing down the query.
It will always result in a fast execution due to optimization.
It allows SQL Server to use the clustered index more effectively.
It increases the likelihood of deadlocks.
questions.correct_answer: It can cause a full table scan, potentially slowing down the query.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of using a clustered index on a primary key column?
choices: It ensures that the data in the table is stored in a physically contiguous manner, improving access speed.
It requires less disk space than a non-clustered index.
It allows for faster updates and deletions.
It eliminates the need for additional indexes on the table.
questions.correct_answer: It ensures that the data in the table is stored in a physically contiguous manner, improving access speed.

questions.question_text: What is the benefit of using the INCLUDE clause in a non-clustered index in SQL Server?
choices: It allows additional columns to be included in the index, reducing the need for lookups to the main table.
It decreases the size of the index, improving performance.
It forces SQL Server to use the index for all queries.
It allows the index to be used for sorting data.
questions.correct_answer: It allows additional columns to be included in the index, reducing the need for lookups to the main table.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential drawback of creating too many indexes on a table?
choices: It can slow down insert, update, and delete operations due to the overhead of maintaining the indexes.
It improves query performance by increasing the number of available execution plans.
It decreases the size of the database by requiring less storage space.
It simplifies query optimization by reducing the number of possible execution plans.
questions.correct_answer: It can slow down insert, update, and delete operations due to the overhead of maintaining the indexes.
questions.explanation: While indexes can improve query performance for SELECT statements, they add overhead to write operations because the indexes must be updated as well.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature automatically adjusts the storage and memory resources allocated to a query based on its execution requirements?
Which of the following techniques can help reduce the amount of disk I/O required by a query?
Which of the following is a reason to use the INCLUDE clause in an index?
choices: To add non-key columns to the index, making it a covering index and reducing the need to access the actual table.
To force SQL Server to use the index for all queries.
To allow the index to be used for sorting data.
To decrease the size of the index.
questions.correct_answer: To add non-key columns to the index, making it a covering index and reducing the need to access the actual table.

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features helps in maintaining consistent performance by automatically identifying and correcting potential query performance issues?
Which of the following techniques can improve the performance of a query that involves a large number of joins?
choices: Using indexes on the join columns
Using SELECT * to retrieve all columns
Using cursors to process the data row by row
Adding an ORDER BY clause to the query
questions.correct_answer: Using indexes on the join columns

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server tools provides a graphical view of query performance, including execution plans and resource usage?
choices: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) Execution Plan
questions.correct_answer: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) Execution Plan

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an effective way to improve the performance of queries that retrieve large result sets?
choices: Using pagination to limit the number of rows returned at one time
Using SELECT * to retrieve all columns
Using cursors to process the data row by row
questions.correct_answer: Using pagination to limit the number of rows returned at one time

questions.question_text: Which SQL clause can be used to limit the number of rows returned by a query, improving performance?
What is the impact of using the OPTION (FORCE ORDER) query hint in SQL Server?
choices: It forces SQL Server to process the joins in the order they appear in the query.
It forces SQL Server to use the most efficient execution plan.
It prevents SQL Server from using any indexes.
It increases the likelihood of a full table scan.
questions.correct_answer: It forces SQL Server to process the joins in the order they appear in the query.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scenarios would benefit most from the use of a filtered index?
choices: A table with a large number of NULL values in a column that is frequently queried for non-NULL values
A table with uniform data distribution across all rows
A table that only has SELECT queries with no updates
A table that has a high volume of insert operations
questions.correct_answer: A table with a large number of NULL values in a column that is frequently queried for non-NULL values

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using a covering index in SQL Server?
choices: It eliminates the need for SQL Server to access the base table, improving query performance.
It reduces the disk space required by the index.
It increases the flexibility of query optimization.
It allows SQL Server to automatically tune the query.
questions.correct_answer: It eliminates the need for SQL Server to access the base table, improving query performance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an effective way to reduce the impact of deadlocks in SQL Server?
choices: Using shorter transactions to minimize the time locks are held
Increasing the isolation level to SERIALIZABLE
Using cursors to process data row by row
Disabling indexes on frequently updated tables
questions.correct_answer: Using shorter transactions to minimize the time locks are held

questions.question_text: What is the primary difference between a stored procedure and a user-defined function in SQL Server?
choices: A stored procedure can return multiple values, while a function can only return a single value
A stored procedure is executed with the EXEC command, while a function is invoked within a query
A stored procedure can only be used for data retrieval, while a function can modify data
A stored procedure can be used within a query, while a function cannot
questions.correct_answer: A stored procedure is executed with the EXEC command, while a function is invoked within a query

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a valid way to create a stored procedure in SQL Server?
choices: CREATE PROCEDURE GetEmployeeDetails AS SELECT * FROM Employees;
EXEC PROCEDURE GetEmployeeDetails AS SELECT * FROM Employees;
SELECT PROCEDURE GetEmployeeDetails AS SELECT * FROM Employees;
INSERT PROCEDURE GetEmployeeDetails AS SELECT * FROM Employees;
questions.correct_answer: CREATE PROCEDURE GetEmployeeDetails AS SELECT * FROM Employees;

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using stored procedures in SQL Server?
choices: They improve performance by reducing network traffic
They allow dynamic SQL to be executed on the client side
They can be executed on any database server without modification
They automatically update indexes on the tables they interact with
questions.correct_answer: They improve performance by reducing network traffic

questions.question_text: Which keyword is used to create a scalar-valued function in SQL Server?
What is a table-valued function in SQL Server?
choices: A function that returns a table data type
A function that returns a single scalar value
A function that modifies data in a table
A function that can only be used in stored procedures
questions.correct_answer: A function that returns a table data type

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about stored procedures?
choices: Stored procedures can accept input parameters
Stored procedures cannot be modified once created
Stored procedures must always return a value
Stored procedures are only used for SELECT statements
questions.correct_answer: Stored procedures can accept input parameters

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using user-defined functions in SQL Server?
choices: They can be reused in multiple queries to encapsulate logic
They can be executed on the client side to reduce server load
They automatically create indexes on the columns they reference
They improve the security of the database by encrypting data
questions.correct_answer: They can be reused in multiple queries to encapsulate logic

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the RETURN statement in a scalar-valued function?
choices: To return a single scalar value from the function
To exit the function without returning a value
To execute a stored procedure within the function
To modify data in the database
questions.correct_answer: To return a single scalar value from the function

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common use case for a table-valued function?
choices: To join the results of the function with other tables
To update rows in a table based on specific criteria
To execute dynamic SQL within the function
To create a new database schema
questions.correct_answer: To join the results of the function with other tables

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a more efficient way to reuse logic in multiple queries?
choices: Copying and pasting the SQL code into each query
Using dynamic SQL within each query
Creating a temporary table to store intermediate results
questions.explanation: User-defined functions allow you to encapsulate and reuse logic in multiple queries, improving code maintainability and efficiency.

questions.question_text: True or False: A stored procedure can return multiple result sets.
Which of the following is a valid reason to use a stored procedure instead of inline SQL?
choices: To improve security by encapsulating logic and controlling access
To increase the complexity of query optimization
To allow users to modify the procedure without permissions
To reduce the performance of frequently executed queries
questions.correct_answer: To improve security by encapsulating logic and controlling access

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to modify an existing stored procedure?
What is the effect of using the WITH ENCRYPTION option when creating a stored procedure?
choices: It encrypts the definition of the stored procedure, preventing users from viewing the code.
It encrypts the data returned by the stored procedure.
It forces the stored procedure to run with elevated privileges.
It requires a password to execute the stored procedure.
questions.correct_answer: It encrypts the definition of the stored procedure, preventing users from viewing the code.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common use case for a scalar-valued function?
choices: Returning a single value based on input parameters, such as calculating a discount
questions.correct_answer: Returning a single value based on input parameters, such as calculating a discount

questions.question_text: True or False: A table-valued function can be used in the FROM clause of a SELECT statement.
Which of the following is a potential drawback of using stored procedures?
choices: They can become complex and difficult to maintain over time.

questions.question_text: Which SQL keyword is used to start a transaction?
What is the purpose of the COMMIT statement in SQL Server?

To roll back the transaction and undo all changes

questions.question_text: Which SQL statement is used to undo all changes made in a transaction?

questions.question_text: Which isolation level ensures that a transaction can read only committed data?

choices: A situation where two or more transactions are waiting for each other to release locks, causing them to be stuck
A process to backup the database
A method to join multiple tables together
A command to rollback a transaction
questions.correct_answer: A situation where two or more transactions are waiting for each other to release locks, causing them to be stuck

questions.question_text: Which of the following can help prevent deadlocks?

Reducing the size of the database

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to explicitly lock a row or table in SQL Server?

To create an index on a table

questions.question_text: Which isolation level ensures that once a row is read by a transaction, it cannot be changed by other transactions until the first transaction is complete?

What is the difference between a COMMIT and a ROLLBACK statement?

COMMIT starts a new transaction, while ROLLBACK ends it

questions.correct_answer: COMMIT saves all changes made in a transaction, while ROLLBACK undoes all changes

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential consequence of using the READ UNCOMMITTED isolation level?
choices: Dirty reads, where a transaction reads data that has not yet been committed
Deadlocks, where transactions are stuck waiting for each other
Increased database size due to additional locking
questions.correct_answer: Dirty reads, where a transaction reads data that has not yet been committed

questions.question_text: What is a phantom read in SQL Server?
choices: A situation where a transaction re-reads data and finds rows that were not there previously
A method to rollback a transaction
A command to backup the database
questions.correct_answer: A situation where a transaction re-reads data and finds rows that were not there previously

questions.question_text: Which isolation level can prevent phantom reads?
What is the purpose of the XLOCK hint in SQL Server?
choices: To take an exclusive lock on a table or row, preventing other transactions from accessing it
questions.correct_answer: To take an exclusive lock on a table or row, preventing other transactions from accessing it

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to view the current locks held by active transactions?
What is the main benefit of using the SNAPSHOT isolation level?

It ensures that no data is ever lost
It speeds up the retrieval of rows from a table
questions.correct_answer: It provides a consistent view of the data without locking, reducing contention between transactions

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a potential drawback of using the SERIALIZABLE isolation level?

It prevents the creation of indexes
questions.correct_answer: It can lead to decreased concurrency and increased locking, potentially slowing down the system

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the NOLOCK hint in SQL Server?
choices: To allow a query to read data without acquiring locks, potentially increasing performance but risking dirty reads
To lock a row or table exclusively
questions.correct_answer: To allow a query to read data without acquiring locks, potentially increasing performance but risking dirty reads

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature automatically detects and resolves deadlocks by choosing one transaction as a victim?
What is the purpose of the TRANSACTION log in SQL Server?
choices: To record all changes made to the database, allowing recovery in case of failure
questions.correct_answer: To record all changes made to the database, allowing recovery in case of failure

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to end a transaction and permanently save all changes?
Which of the following is a key feature of the SERIALIZABLE isolation level?
choices: It prevents other transactions from reading or writing to the data until the transaction is complete
It reduces locking and increases concurrency
questions.correct_answer: It prevents other transactions from reading or writing to the data until the transaction is complete

questions.question_text: What does the SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL statement do in SQL Server?
choices: It sets the isolation level for the current session, determining how transactions interact with each other
It creates an index on a table
questions.correct_answer: It sets the isolation level for the current session, determining how transactions interact with each other

questions.question_text: Which SQL statement is used to manually end a transaction and discard all changes made?
What is the primary purpose of SQL Server authentication?

To manage permissions for database objects
To encrypt data stored in the database
questions.correct_answer: To verify the identity of users trying to connect to the SQL Server

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of SQL Server Windows Authentication?
choices: It uses Active Directory to authenticate users
It requires a separate username and password for SQL Server
It is less secure than SQL Server Authentication
It does not support encrypted connections
questions.correct_answer: It uses Active Directory to authenticate users

questions.question_text: What is the role of a SQL Server login?
choices: To provide access to SQL Server at the instance level
To manage user permissions within a specific database
questions.correct_answer: To provide access to SQL Server at the instance level

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to manage user permissions on database objects?
What is a SQL Server role?
choices: A collection of permissions that can be assigned to users
A database schema used to organize objects
A set of tables and views used to store data
A process that automatically backs up databases
questions.correct_answer: A collection of permissions that can be assigned to users

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of using roles in SQL Server?
choices: They simplify the management of user permissions
They reduce the need for database backups
questions.correct_answer: They simplify the management of user permissions

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the GRANT statement in SQL Server?
choices: To assign permissions to users or roles
To remove permissions from users or roles
questions.correct_answer: To assign permissions to users or roles

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to encrypt data at rest?
What is the purpose of SQL Server auditing?
choices: To track and log activities and changes within the database
To manage user roles and permissions
questions.correct_answer: To track and log activities and changes within the database

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature provides encryption for specific columns within a database?
What is the role of a SQL Server certificate?
choices: To support encryption of data at rest and in transit
questions.correct_answer: To support encryption of data at rest and in transit

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a security best practice for SQL Server?
choices: Using SQL Server Authentication for all users
Allowing unrestricted access to all users

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server roles?
choices: To manage user permissions and access to database objects
questions.correct_answer: To manage user permissions and access to database objects

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of SQL Server encryption?
choices: It protects sensitive data from unauthorized access
It reduces the size of the database
questions.correct_answer: It protects sensitive data from unauthorized access

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a function of SQL Server's Row-Level Security?
choices: It restricts access to rows in a database table based on the characteristics of the user executing a query
It encrypts data at rest in the database
It tracks and logs database activities
questions.correct_answer: It restricts access to rows in a database table based on the characteristics of the user executing a query

questions.question_text: What does the SQL Server REVOKE statement do?
choices: It removes previously granted permissions from a user or role
It grants new permissions to a user or role
It creates a new database role
questions.correct_answer: It removes previously granted permissions from a user or role

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Data Masking feature?
choices: To obfuscate sensitive data by displaying masked values instead of actual data to unauthorized users
To encrypt data in the database
questions.correct_answer: To obfuscate sensitive data by displaying masked values instead of actual data to unauthorized users

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to limit the visibility of specific rows to specific users?
What is the purpose of SQL Server's Logins?
choices: To control access to SQL Server at the instance level
To manage permissions within a database
questions.correct_answer: To control access to SQL Server at the instance level

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common use of SQL Server's Schema permissions?
choices: To manage access to groups of database objects within a schema
To encrypt data in the database
questions.correct_answer: To manage access to groups of database objects within a schema

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows for encryption of data both at rest and in transit?
What is the main advantage of SQL Server's Always Encrypted feature?
choices: It ensures that sensitive data is always encrypted both in storage and in use, even during query processing.
It automatically compresses data to save space.
It allows SQL Server to execute queries faster.
It improves the readability of complex queries.
questions.correct_answer: It ensures that sensitive data is always encrypted both in storage and in use, even during query processing.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)?
choices: To encrypt an entire database to protect data at rest
To encrypt individual columns within a database
To create encrypted backups of the database
questions.correct_answer: To encrypt an entire database to protect data at rest

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a security best practice when creating SQL Server logins?
choices: Use complex passwords that include a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
Use simple passwords to make them easy to remember.
Reuse the same password across all logins.
questions.correct_answer: Use complex passwords that include a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

questions.question_text: What is the role of SQL Server's Database Users?
choices: To define permissions within a specific database
To control access to SQL Server at the instance level
To encrypt data within the database
questions.correct_answer: To define permissions within a specific database

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows for defining and enforcing policies across multiple SQL Server instances?
Which of the following is a feature of SQL Server's Audit Logs?
choices: They capture and store information about events that occur in the SQL Server instance, such as changes to data or permissions.

questions.correct_answer: They capture and store information about events that occur in the SQL Server instance, such as changes to data or permissions.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's Security Principals?
choices: To represent entities that can request SQL Server resources, such as logins, users, and roles.
To encrypt data within the database.
To create and manage database triggers.
questions.correct_answer: To represent entities that can request SQL Server resources, such as logins, users, and roles.

questions.question_text: What is the benefit of using SQL Server's Always Encrypted feature in a multi-tenant environment?
choices: It ensures that sensitive data remains encrypted and cannot be accessed by unauthorized tenants, even if they share the same database.
It improves the performance of the database.
It allows SQL Server to handle larger volumes of data.
It simplifies the management of user permissions.
questions.correct_answer: It ensures that sensitive data remains encrypted and cannot be accessed by unauthorized tenants, even if they share the same database.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for managing SQL Server permissions?
choices: Use the principle of least privilege, granting users only the permissions they need to perform their tasks.
Grant all users full administrative privileges.
Disable all security features to simplify management.
Reuse the same set of permissions for all users, regardless of their roles.
questions.correct_answer: Use the principle of least privilege, granting users only the permissions they need to perform their tasks.

questions.question_text: What is the role of SQL Server's Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)?
choices: To assign permissions to roles, which can then be assigned to users, simplifying the management of user permissions.
To encrypt data in the database.
To create and manage database triggers.
questions.correct_answer: To assign permissions to roles, which can then be assigned to users, simplifying the management of user permissions.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a database backup?
choices: To create a copy of the database that can be restored in case of data loss
To improve the performance of the database
questions.correct_answer: To create a copy of the database that can be restored in case of data loss

questions.question_text: Which of the following backup types captures only the data that has changed since the last full backup?
What is the main advantage of using a transaction log backup in SQL Server?
choices: It allows for point-in-time recovery by capturing the sequence of transactions.
It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.
It compresses the database to save space.
It improves the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: It allows for point-in-time recovery by capturing the sequence of transactions.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature is used to automate the scheduling of backups?
What is the purpose of a copy-only backup?
choices: To create a backup without affecting the sequence of conventional backups.
To create a backup that includes all data and schema changes.
To compress the backup file to save space.
questions.correct_answer: To create a backup without affecting the sequence of conventional backups.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a full database backup?
choices: It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.
It only captures changes made since the last backup.
It compresses the database to save space.
It only captures the transaction log.
questions.correct_answer: It captures the entire database, including all data and schema.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of log shipping in SQL Server?
choices: To automatically send transaction log backups to a secondary server for disaster recovery.
To compress database logs to save space.
To manage user permissions across multiple databases.
To encrypt data in transit between servers.
questions.correct_answer: To automatically send transaction log backups to a secondary server for disaster recovery.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to restore a database to a specific point in time?
What is the primary purpose of a restore operation in SQL Server?
choices: To recover a database to a previous state in case of data loss or corruption.
To improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: To recover a database to a previous state in case of data loss or corruption.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for database backups?
choices: Store backups in a secure, off-site location.
Store backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
questions.correct_answer: Store backups in a secure, off-site location.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's backup compression feature?
choices: To reduce the size of the backup file, saving storage space.
To improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: To reduce the size of the backup file, saving storage space.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to restore specific pages of a database instead of the entire database?
Which of the following is a benefit of using differential backups?
choices: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the RESTORE VERIFYONLY command in SQL Server?
choices: To verify that a backup can be read and is not corrupted, without actually restoring it.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
To compress the backup file to save space.
questions.correct_answer: To verify that a backup can be read and is not corrupted, without actually restoring it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using backup encryption in SQL Server?
choices: It protects backup data from unauthorized access.
It improves the performance of queries.
It reduces the size of the backup file.
questions.correct_answer: It protects backup data from unauthorized access.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using differential backups in combination with full backups?
choices: They provide faster recovery times by allowing you to restore only the changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: They provide faster recovery times by allowing you to restore only the changes since the last full backup.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for ensuring the reliability of database backups?
choices: Regularly test backups by restoring them to a separate environment.
Store backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
questions.correct_answer: Regularly test backups by restoring them to a separate environment.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's tail-log backup?
choices: To capture any transactions that occurred since the last transaction log backup, ensuring that no data is lost during the restore process.
To compress the backup file to save space.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
questions.correct_answer: To capture any transactions that occurred since the last transaction log backup, ensuring that no data is lost during the restore process.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows you to create a backup of the transaction log?
Which of the following is a common use case for SQL Server's filegroup backup?
choices: To backup only specific filegroups in a database, reducing the size and time required for the backup.
To backup the entire database, including all data and schema.
To improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: To backup only specific filegroups in a database, reducing the size and time required for the backup.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of SQL Server's backup retention policy?
choices: To define how long backups should be kept before they are deleted, helping to manage storage space.
To improve the performance of backups.
To compress the backup file to save space.
questions.correct_answer: To define how long backups should be kept before they are deleted, helping to manage storage space.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a best practice for database recovery planning?
choices: Regularly update and test the recovery plan to ensure it meets current business needs.
Store all backups on the same server as the database.
Disable all backups to improve performance.
Reuse the same backup file for all backups.
questions.correct_answer: Regularly update and test the recovery plan to ensure it meets current business needs.

questions.question_text: Which SQL Server feature allows for the creation of a backup strategy that includes full, differential, and transaction log backups?
What is the purpose of the SQL Server RESTORE HEADERONLY command?
choices: To return information about the backup, such as the backup start and end time, without actually restoring the data.
To restore the entire database to a previous state.
To compress the backup file to save space.
questions.correct_answer: To return information about the backup, such as the backup start and end time, without actually restoring the data.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a benefit of using SQL Server's backup compression feature?
choices: It reduces the size of the backup file, saving storage space and potentially speeding up the backup process.
It improves the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: It reduces the size of the backup file, saving storage space and potentially speeding up the backup process.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using log shipping in SQL Server?
choices: It provides an automated way to maintain a standby server that can take over in case of primary server failure, ensuring high availability.
It improves the performance of queries.
It compresses the database logs to save space.
questions.correct_answer: It provides an automated way to maintain a standby server that can take over in case of primary server failure, ensuring high availability.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of SQL Server's backup encryption feature?
choices: To protect backup data from unauthorized access.
To compress the backup file to save space.
To improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: To protect backup data from unauthorized access.

questions.question_text: Which of the following SQL Server features allows you to automate the backup and recovery process?
What is the benefit of using differential backups in SQL Server?
choices: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.
They capture the entire database, including all data and schema.
They improve the performance of queries.
questions.correct_answer: They reduce the time and storage space required for backups by only capturing changes since the last full backup.

quizzes.quiz_name: Power BI DAX: A to Z Comprehensive and Concise

questions.question_text: What is Power BI primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Power BI is a data visualization tool that allows users to create interactive dashboards and reports.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI is available in Desktop, Service, and Mobile versions.
questions.explanation: Power BI is available as Power BI Desktop (for creating reports), Power BI Service (for sharing and collaborating), and Power BI Mobile (for accessing reports on the go).

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Power BI can connect to various ______ including Excel, SQL Server, and web data sources.
questions.explanation: Power BI supports connections to a wide range of data sources, making it a versatile tool for data analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a component of Power BI?
questions.explanation: Power BI Server is not a component of Power BI. The main components are Power BI Desktop, Gateway, and Service.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI Desktop is used for report creation and data modeling.
questions.explanation: Power BI Desktop is the primary tool used for creating reports and data models in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: Power BI Mobile allows users to access their reports on ______.
questions.explanation: Power BI Mobile provides access to reports and dashboards on mobile devices, ensuring data is available on the go.

questions.question_text: Match the following Power BI components with their descriptions.

definitions: Used for creating reports and data models
Used for sharing and collaboration
Used for accessing reports on the go

correct_answer.Power BI Desktop: Used for creating reports and data models
correct_answer.Power BI Mobile: Used for accessing reports on the go

questions.explanation: Understanding the different components of Power BI is crucial for effectively using the tool.

questions.question_text:
Explain the role of Power BI Gateway.

Which statement best answers this?
choices: Creating a data model involves identifying key tables, defining relationships between them, and creating measures that will be used in your analysis.
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is used to compare the performance of a measure, such as revenue, against the same period in the previous year.
Cohort Analysis groups employees by hire date and tracks their retention over time.

questions.explanation: Power BI Gateway is used to connect on-premises data sources to Power BI, enabling cloud-based reports to access on-premises data.

questions.question_text: Which Power BI component is primarily used for real-time dashboards?
questions.explanation: Power BI Service is used for hosting and managing real-time dashboards and reports.

questions.question_text: True or False: Power BI can only connect to structured data sources.
questions.explanation: Power BI can connect to both structured and unstructured data sources, providing flexibility in data analysis.

questions.question_text: What does DAX stand for?
questions.explanation: DAX stands for Data Analysis Expressions, the formula language used in Power BI, Power Pivot, and SQL Server Analysis Services.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX is only used in Power BI.
questions.explanation: DAX is also used in Power Pivot for Excel and SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS), not just Power BI.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: DAX allows users to create ______ columns and measures in Power BI.
questions.explanation: Calculated columns and measures are created using DAX to perform calculations on data in Power BI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key feature of DAX?
questions.explanation: DAX supports iterative calculations, allowing complex operations to be performed on data row by row.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX can perform both row-level and aggregated calculations.
questions.explanation: DAX can perform calculations at both the row level (e.g., using SUMX) and the aggregated level (e.g., using SUM).

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: A DAX ______ is a pre-defined calculation that can be used in a Power BI report.
questions.explanation: A DAX measure is a pre-defined calculation, such as SUM(Sales[Amount]), that can be reused in reports.

questions.question_text: Match the following DAX functions with their uses.

definitions: Calculates the total of a column
Calculates the mean value of a column
Counts the number of rows

correct_answer.SUM: Calculates the total of a column
correct_answer.AVERAGE: Calculates the mean value of a column

questions.explanation: These basic DAX functions are used to perform common calculations in Power BI.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a calculated column in Power BI?
questions.explanation: Calculated columns are used to perform calculations at the row level, such as calculating a total for each sale.

questions.question_text: True or False: DAX is a case-sensitive language.
questions.explanation: DAX is not case-sensitive; 'SUM' and 'sum' are treated the same.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The ______ function in DAX is used to apply logic, returning different results based on a condition.
questions.explanation: The IF function is used to apply conditional logic in DAX, similar to how it's used in Excel.

questions.question_text: Which of the following DAX formulas correctly calculates the total sales from a 'Sales' table?
questions.explanation: The correct formula is SUM(Sales[Total]), which adds up all the values in the 'Total' column of the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: True or False: The formula SUMX(Sales, Sales[Amount] * Sales[Quantity]) calculates the total revenue by multiplying 'Amount' by 'Quantity' for each row and then summing the results.
questions.explanation: SUMX is an iterator function that processes row by row and calculates 'Sales[Amount] * Sales[Quantity]' for each row before summing the results.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX formula to calculate the average sales amount per transaction is ______.
questions.explanation: AVERAGE(Sales[Amount]) calculates the mean value of the 'Amount' column in the 'Sales' table.

questions.question_text: True or False: The following formula returns the first non-blank value in the 'Date' column: FIRSTNONBLANK(Sales[Date], Sales[Amount]).

questions.question_text: True or False: Power Query is the tool used in Power BI for data transformation.

lessons.lesson_name: 5.3 DAX for Operational and HR Analytics

questions.question_text: You need to calculate the employee turnover rate for your company. Which of the following DAX formulas would you use?
questions.explanation: The turnover rate is calculated by dividing the number of terminated employees by the total number of employees, using CALCULATE to filter for terminated employees.

questions.question_text: True or False: The DAX function AVERAGEX can be used to calculate the average tenure of employees within the company.
questions.explanation: AVERAGEX can be used to calculate the average tenure by evaluating the difference between hire date and termination date (or current date) for each employee.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ can be used to calculate the headcount of employees at the end of each month.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE combined with LASTDATE is often used to calculate the headcount by filtering the data to the last date of each month and counting active employees.

questions.question_text: Which DAX pattern would you use to calculate the number of hours worked by employees in a specific department over a given period?
questions.explanation: This pattern uses SUMX to sum the hours worked by employees, filtered by the specific department.

questions.question_text: True or False: The 'Cohort Analysis' DAX pattern is useful in HR analytics for analyzing the retention rate of employees hired in the same period.
questions.explanation: Cohort Analysis is a DAX pattern that groups employees by their hire date and tracks their retention over time, which is useful in HR analytics.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The DAX function ______ is commonly used to calculate the total compensation for employees, including bonuses and benefits.
questions.explanation: SUMX is used to calculate total compensation by summing up the base salary, bonuses, and benefits for each employee.

questions.question_text: Match the following HR DAX patterns with their applications.

definitions: Measures the rate at which employees leave the company.
Tracks employee retention over time.
Calculates the number of active employees at a specific point in time.

questions.explanation: These HR analytics patterns are essential for managing and analyzing employee data in Power BI.

questions.question_text: For the capstone project, you are required to build a comprehensive Power BI report. Which of the following steps should you start with?

Avoid using measures and use calculated columns instead

Use calculated columns instead of measures
Apply filters directly to high cardinality columns

questions.question_text: True or False: The CROSSJOIN function in DAX is used to return all combinations of rows between two tables.

Calculates the year-to-date total of a measure

questions.question_text: Which function assigns a unique sequential number to every row with no ties?
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique sequential values regardless of ties.

questions.question_text: RANK() is applied to salaries 9000, 8000, 8000, 7000. What rank does 7000 receive?
questions.explanation: Two rows share rank 2, so rank 3 is skipped and 7000 receives rank 4.

questions.question_text: Which clause inside OVER() restarts ranking per department?
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY resets the window function for each partition group.

questions.question_text: Which function looks at the PREVIOUS row's value within a window?
questions.explanation: LAG() retrieves a value from a prior row; LEAD() retrieves from a following row.

questions.question_text: LAST_VALUE() without a frame clause returns incorrect results because:
choices: It only looks up to the current row by default
questions.correct_answer: It only looks up to the current row by default
questions.explanation: Default frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so LAST_VALUE sees only up to the current row.

questions.question_text: Fill the blank: SELECT Name, ___(Sales,1) OVER (ORDER BY Month) AS PrevSales FROM Sales
questions.explanation: LAG looks back one row; LEAD looks forward.

questions.question_text: DENSE_RANK() skips rank numbers after a tie.
questions.explanation: DENSE_RANK() never skips — that is RANK().

questions.question_text: NTILE(4) on 8 rows assigns bucket numbers:
questions.explanation: NTILE divides rows evenly across buckets in order.

questions.question_text: ROW_NUMBER() can produce the same value for two rows in the same partition.
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique values — ties are broken arbitrarily.

questions.question_text: To get the top earner per department you wrap a ROW_NUMBER() query and filter:
questions.explanation: Filtering rn=1 in the outer query returns one row per partition.

questions.question_text: FIRST_VALUE(Sales) OVER (PARTITION BY Dept ORDER BY Month) always returns:
choices: The first month's sales for that department
questions.correct_answer: The first month's sales for that department
questions.explanation: FIRST_VALUE returns the first value in the ordered partition.

questions.question_text: The keyword that separates window functions into groups is ___.
questions.explanation: PARTITION BY resets the window per group.

questions.question_text: Which frame clause makes LAST_VALUE() return the true last value in a partition?
choices: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
questions.correct_answer: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
questions.explanation: This extends the frame to cover all rows in the partition.

questions.question_text: LAG() returns NULL for the first row because there is no previous row.
questions.explanation: With no prior row, LAG returns NULL unless a default is specified.

questions.question_text: Sales growth = current month minus previous month. Which expression is correct?
questions.explanation: LAG gives the previous row's Sales; subtracting gives the growth.

questions.question_text: Which application do you open to write and run T-SQL window functions against SQL Server?
questions.explanation: SSMS is the primary IDE for SQL Server T-SQL development.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, where do you type your SQL query?
questions.explanation: The Query Editor is the central text area where you write T-SQL.

questions.question_text: What keyboard shortcut executes a query in SSMS?
questions.explanation: F5 (or clicking Execute) runs the selected or entire query in SSMS.

questions.question_text: How do you open a new query window in SSMS?
choices: File > New > Query with Current Connection
Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
questions.correct_answer: Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
questions.explanation: Both methods open a fresh query editor tab connected to the current server.

questions.question_text: Where do you see query results after pressing F5 in SSMS?
choices: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
questions.explanation: Results appear in the bottom pane; the Messages tab shows row counts and errors.

questions.question_text: To switch to a different database inside SSMS, what are your two options?
choices: Only the database dropdown at the top toolbar
USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
questions.correct_answer: USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
questions.explanation: Both methods work — the dropdown is quicker for ad hoc work.

questions.question_text: Where do you find existing stored procedures for a database in SSMS Object Explorer?
questions.explanation: Expand your database node, then Programmability, then Stored Procedures.

questions.question_text: How do you view and edit an existing stored procedure in SSMS?
choices: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
You must DROP and recreate it
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
questions.explanation: Right-click > Modify opens a query window pre-populated with ALTER PROCEDURE.

questions.question_text: How do you save a T-SQL script in SSMS?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S saves your query to a local .sql file you can reopen later.

questions.question_text: How do you call (execute) a stored procedure with parameters in T-SQL?
questions.explanation: EXEC (or EXECUTE) followed by the procedure name and named parameters is the correct syntax.

questions.question_text: To see the actual execution plan for a query in SSMS, what do you do?
choices: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
Open a new window and type EXPLAIN
questions.correct_answer: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
questions.explanation: Ctrl+M toggles 'Include Actual Execution Plan' — the plan tab appears after you run the query.

questions.question_text: After writing a CREATE PROCEDURE statement in SSMS, what must you do to save it to the database?
choices: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
Both Ctrl+S and F5 are required
questions.correct_answer: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
questions.explanation: Running CREATE PROCEDURE registers it in the database. Ctrl+S only saves the script file locally.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, pressing F5 with text selected will execute only the selected text, not the entire script.
questions.explanation: If you highlight a portion of the query before pressing F5, only that portion runs.

questions.question_text: You can only have one Query Editor tab open at a time in SSMS.
questions.explanation: SSMS supports multiple tabbed Query Editor windows simultaneously.

lessons.lesson_name: Module 2 – CTE, Temp Tables & Table Variables

questions.question_text: What keyword starts a CTE?
questions.explanation: CTEs begin with the WITH keyword followed by the CTE name.

questions.question_text: A recursive CTE must contain:
choices: An anchor member UNION ALL a recursive member
Two SELECT statements joined by UNION
questions.correct_answer: An anchor member UNION ALL a recursive member
questions.explanation: The anchor provides the starting rows; the recursive part joins back to the CTE.

questions.question_text: Which temp table type is visible to ALL active sessions?
questions.explanation: ## prefix makes the table visible across all sessions.

questions.question_text: A @TableVariable does NOT support:
questions.explanation: Table variables have no statistics, leading to poor cardinality estimates on large sets.

questions.question_text: When does a #Temp table get automatically dropped?
questions.explanation: #Temp tables persist for the entire session and are dropped when the connection closes.

questions.question_text: A CTE can be referenced multiple times in the same query.
questions.explanation: Unlike a subquery, a CTE can be referenced more than once in the query that defines it.

questions.question_text: Fill: WITH ___ AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM ___
questions.explanation: The CTE name is used both in the definition and the reference.

questions.question_text: A @TableVariable rolls back when a ROLLBACK TRANSACTION is issued.
questions.explanation: Table variable changes survive a ROLLBACK — useful for error logging.

questions.question_text: Which is best for large intermediate datasets that need an index?
questions.explanation: Temp tables support indexes and statistics unlike table variables or CTEs.

questions.question_text: The recursive part of a CTE joins the table back to the ___ itself.
questions.explanation: The recursive member references the CTE by name to process the next level.

questions.question_text: What happens to a ##GlobalTemp table when the last session using it closes?
questions.explanation: Global temp tables are dropped when no session is referencing them.

questions.question_text: A CTE can persist data across multiple separate queries.
questions.explanation: A CTE exists only for the duration of the single query in which it is defined.

questions.question_text: A CTE vs subquery: the key readability advantage of a CTE is:
choices: It is named and defined once at the top, making complex queries easier to read
It runs faster than a subquery
questions.correct_answer: It is named and defined once at the top, making complex queries easier to read
questions.explanation: CTEs improve readability by naming the logic and separating it from the main query.

questions.question_text: In the org chart recursive CTE, Level + 1 means:
choices: Calculate the child's depth by adding 1 to the parent's depth
questions.correct_answer: Calculate the child's depth by adding 1 to the parent's depth
questions.explanation: Each recursive round adds 1 to the parent Level so children get the correct depth.

questions.question_text: Inside a stored procedure, a #Temp table created in the procedure is dropped when the procedure finishes.
questions.explanation: Temp tables created inside a stored procedure are scoped to that procedure and dropped on exit.

questions.question_text: Where in SSMS do you write a CTE?
choices: In the Stored Procedures node only
In any Query Editor window — CTEs are written inline before the main SELECT
questions.correct_answer: In any Query Editor window — CTEs are written inline before the main SELECT
questions.explanation: CTEs are part of a T-SQL statement and written in the query editor, not stored separately.

questions.question_text: You created a #temp table in one query window. Can you see it in a second new query window in SSMS?
choices: Yes, all windows share temp tables
No — #temp tables are session-scoped; a new window is a new session
Yes if you use the same login
questions.correct_answer: No — #temp tables are session-scoped; a new window is a new session
questions.explanation: Each SSMS query window has its own session. #temp tables are not visible across sessions.

questions.question_text: Where do you see temporary tables listed in SSMS Object Explorer?
choices: Under System Databases > tempdb > Temporary Tables
They are invisible in Object Explorer
questions.correct_answer: Under System Databases > tempdb > Temporary Tables
