questions.explanation: Temp tables live in tempdb and appear there in Object Explorer while the session is active.

questions.question_text: How do you explicitly drop a temp table before recreating it in the same script?
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS avoids errors if the table doesn't exist yet — safe to use at the top of scripts.

questions.question_text: A CTE is defined using which keyword at the start?
questions.explanation: Syntax: WITH cte_name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM cte_name;

questions.question_text: In SSMS, if you get the error 'Invalid object name #MyTemp', what is the most likely cause?
choices: The table was created in a different session or was already dropped
You need to prefix it with dbo.
Temp tables require a special permission
The table name has too many characters
questions.correct_answer: The table was created in a different session or was already dropped
questions.explanation: #temp tables are session-scoped and auto-drop when the session ends.

questions.question_text: How do you run only part of a script in SSMS — for example, just the CTE section?
choices: Highlight the text you want to run, then press F5
SSMS always runs the full script
questions.correct_answer: Highlight the text you want to run, then press F5
questions.explanation: Selecting text before F5 restricts execution to that selection.

questions.question_text: How do you add a comment explaining a CTE in T-SQL?
choices: /* This is a comment */ or -- single line comment
questions.correct_answer: /* This is a comment */ or -- single line comment
questions.explanation: T-SQL uses -- for single-line and /* */ for multi-line comments.

questions.question_text: What SSMS keyboard shortcut formats/indents selected SQL code?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+K then Ctrl+F auto-formats the selected SQL in SSMS.

questions.question_text: To check whether a temp table already exists before creating it, which pattern do you use?
choices: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tempdb.sys.objects WHERE name LIKE '#MyTemp%') DROP TABLE #MyTemp
questions.correct_answer: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tempdb.sys.objects WHERE name LIKE '#MyTemp%') DROP TABLE #MyTemp
questions.explanation: This checks tempdb system tables for the temp table before dropping.

questions.question_text: Where does a recursive CTE require the MAXRECURSION option to be set if depth exceeds 100?
choices: As a query hint OPTION (MAXRECURSION n) at the end of the final SELECT
questions.correct_answer: As a query hint OPTION (MAXRECURSION n) at the end of the final SELECT
questions.explanation: Add OPTION (MAXRECURSION 0) after the final SELECT to allow unlimited recursion.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, what colour does SSMS highlight SQL keywords like WITH, SELECT, FROM in by default?
questions.explanation: SSMS syntax highlights reserved keywords in blue by default.

questions.question_text: A CTE result can be referenced multiple times in the same query after its WITH block.
questions.explanation: You can SELECT from a CTE as many times as needed within the same query.

questions.question_text: Pressing Ctrl+Z in SSMS undoes changes to the query text in the editor.
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z is standard undo in the SSMS query editor.

questions.question_text: What is a VIEW in SQL Server?
choices: A saved SELECT query stored as a virtual table
A physical copy of a table
A stored procedure with no parameters
questions.correct_answer: A saved SELECT query stored as a virtual table
questions.explanation: A view does not store data — it re-runs its query each time it is accessed.

questions.question_text: Which keyword is required when creating an Indexed View?
questions.explanation: SCHEMABINDING locks the underlying table schema so the view cannot break if columns change.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a Stored Procedure and a Function?
choices: A function cannot modify data; a stored procedure can
A stored procedure cannot take parameters
A function can call a stored procedure
questions.correct_answer: A function cannot modify data; a stored procedure can
questions.explanation: Functions are read-only and side-effect free; SPs can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and use transactions.

questions.question_text: An Inline Table-Valued Function requires:
choices: A single RETURN with a SELECT — no BEGIN/END
questions.correct_answer: A single RETURN with a SELECT — no BEGIN/END
questions.explanation: Inline TVFs are treated like parameterised views and have a single RETURN (SELECT).

questions.question_text: To hide the Salary column from a junior analyst, the best approach is:
choices: Create a VIEW that excludes the Salary column and GRANT access to the view only
Use a stored procedure with no salary output
questions.correct_answer: Create a VIEW that excludes the Salary column and GRANT access to the view only
questions.explanation: The view acts as a security layer — the analyst never sees the underlying table.

questions.question_text: You can always UPDATE data through any view.
questions.explanation: Updates through views are only possible on simple single-table views without aggregations.

questions.question_text: Which SQL statement changes an existing view definition?
questions.explanation: ALTER VIEW replaces the view definition without dropping and recreating it.

questions.question_text: A scalar function returns a single ___, while an inline TVF returns a table.
questions.explanation: Scalar functions return one value; TVFs return a result set.

questions.question_text: Which of these CAN be used inside a SELECT statement?
questions.explanation: Functions can appear in SELECT; stored procedures cannot.

questions.question_text: An indexed view physically stores its result set on disk.
questions.explanation: The unique clustered index materialises the view result, making reads faster.

questions.question_text: COUNT_BIG(*) is required in an indexed view because:
choices: GROUP BY in indexed views requires COUNT_BIG(*) not COUNT(*)
questions.correct_answer: GROUP BY in indexed views requires COUNT_BIG(*) not COUNT(*)
questions.explanation: SQL Server enforces COUNT_BIG(*) as a requirement for indexed views with GROUP BY.

questions.question_text: OUTPUT parameters in a stored procedure allow you to:
choices: Pass a value back to the caller
questions.correct_answer: Pass a value back to the caller
questions.explanation: OUTPUT parameters carry a value from inside the SP back to the calling code.

questions.question_text: A stored procedure can call another stored procedure.
questions.explanation: Nested stored procedure calls are fully supported in SQL Server.

questions.question_text: EXEC vs sp_executesql — sp_executesql is preferred for dynamic SQL because:
choices: It supports parameterisation, enabling plan reuse and preventing SQL injection
questions.correct_answer: It supports parameterisation, enabling plan reuse and preventing SQL injection
questions.explanation: Parameterised dynamic SQL via sp_executesql avoids injection and reuses cached plans.

questions.question_text: Which is the correct syntax to execute a stored procedure with a parameter?
questions.explanation: EXEC is the correct keyword; CALL is MySQL syntax.

questions.question_text: In SSMS Object Explorer, where do you find Views for a database?
questions.explanation: Views appear directly under the database node in the Views folder.

questions.question_text: How do you create a new Stored Procedure using the SSMS GUI wizard?
choices: Right-click Stored Procedures > New Stored Procedure — SSMS opens a template in the Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Right-click Stored Procedures > New Stored Procedure — SSMS opens a template in the Query Editor
questions.explanation: SSMS generates a CREATE PROCEDURE template you can fill in.

questions.question_text: After writing CREATE VIEW vw_Name AS SELECT ... in SSMS, what step makes the view actually exist in the database?
questions.explanation: Executing the CREATE VIEW statement compiles it into the database.

questions.question_text: How do you modify an existing view in SSMS without dropping and recreating it?
choices: Right-click the view > Script View as > ALTER To > New Query Window, then edit and run
DELETE the view and rewrite it
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the view > Script View as > ALTER To > New Query Window, then edit and run
questions.explanation: This generates ALTER VIEW which modifies without dropping.

questions.question_text: Where are User-Defined Functions (UDFs) stored in SSMS Object Explorer?
questions.explanation: Functions live under Programmability alongside Stored Procedures.

questions.question_text: To execute a scalar function in SSMS, what is the correct syntax?
questions.explanation: Scalar functions are called inside a SELECT — you must prefix with the schema (dbo.).

questions.question_text: How do you call an Inline Table-Valued Function (TVF) in a query?
questions.explanation: TVFs return a table so you query them in the FROM clause just like a table.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you view the T-SQL definition of an existing stored procedure quickly?
questions.explanation: sp_helptext returns the source code of any stored procedure, view or function.

questions.question_text: What is the keyboard shortcut in SSMS to jump to a specific line number?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+G opens the 'Go to Line' dialog in SSMS.

questions.question_text: How do you test a stored procedure with output parameters in SSMS?
choices: Declare a variable, EXEC the SP passing the variable with OUTPUT keyword, then SELECT the variable
Just EXEC the SP — output parameters print automatically
Output parameters cannot be tested in SSMS
questions.correct_answer: Declare a variable, EXEC the SP passing the variable with OUTPUT keyword, then SELECT the variable
questions.explanation: Pattern: DECLARE @Out INT; EXEC usp_Name @OutParam = @Out OUTPUT; SELECT @Out;

questions.question_text: In SSMS, what does the red underline under a table or column name in the query editor indicate?
choices: The object cannot be found — likely wrong database or typo
questions.correct_answer: The object cannot be found — likely wrong database or typo
questions.explanation: SSMS IntelliSense underlines names it cannot resolve in the current database context.

questions.question_text: How do you refresh the Object Explorer in SSMS after creating new objects?
choices: Right-click the node (e.g. Stored Procedures) > Refresh
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the node (e.g. Stored Procedures) > Refresh
questions.explanation: Right-click > Refresh updates the node to show newly created objects.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, you can drag a table name from Object Explorer into the Query Editor to auto-type the table name.
questions.explanation: Dragging a table or column from Object Explorer inserts its name into the query editor.

questions.question_text: ALTER VIEW requires you to drop the view first before redefining it.
questions.explanation: ALTER VIEW modifies the view in place without dropping it — permissions are preserved.

questions.question_text: Which JOIN returns only rows where a match exists in BOTH tables?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN filters to matched rows only.

questions.question_text: To find customers who have NEVER placed an order, you use:
choices: LEFT JOIN Orders ON ... WHERE Orders.ID IS NULL
questions.correct_answer: LEFT JOIN Orders ON ... WHERE Orders.ID IS NULL
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN brings all customers; IS NULL on the right side finds those with no match.

questions.question_text: A CROSS JOIN of 5 customers and 4 products returns how many rows?
questions.explanation: CROSS JOIN produces a Cartesian product: 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.question_text: EXISTS vs IN — EXISTS is faster on large datasets because:
choices: It stops searching after the first match is found
It retrieves the full list first
questions.correct_answer: It stops searching after the first match is found
questions.explanation: EXISTS short-circuits on the first match; IN must evaluate the entire subquery result.

questions.question_text: A correlated subquery differs from a non-correlated subquery because:
choices: It references a column from the outer query and runs once per outer row
questions.correct_answer: It references a column from the outer query and runs once per outer row
questions.explanation: The reference to the outer query forces the inner query to re-execute per row.

questions.question_text: RIGHT JOIN can always be rewritten as a LEFT JOIN by swapping the tables.
questions.explanation: Swapping table order and changing RIGHT to LEFT produces identical results.

questions.question_text: Which JOIN type would you use to find mismatches on BOTH sides at once?
questions.explanation: FULL OUTER JOIN includes all rows from both tables with NULLs where unmatched.

questions.question_text: A SELF JOIN is used to:
choices: Join a table to itself — e.g. employee to their manager in the same table
questions.correct_answer: Join a table to itself — e.g. employee to their manager in the same table
questions.explanation: SELF JOIN uses two aliases of the same table to create a relationship within it.

questions.question_text: The filter on aggregated results uses ___ not WHERE.
questions.explanation: HAVING is applied after GROUP BY; WHERE is applied before aggregation.

questions.question_text: CASE WHEN Salary >= 80000 THEN 'High' WHEN Salary >= 50000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Low' END — what type is this?
questions.explanation: Searched CASE uses conditions; Simple CASE matches a single value.

questions.question_text: NOT IN breaks silently when the subquery returns any NULL values.
questions.explanation: NOT IN with NULLs in the list returns no rows — use NOT EXISTS to handle NULLs safely.

questions.question_text: To count employees per salary band in one query you use:
choices: COUNT(CASE WHEN Salary>=80000 THEN 1 END) for each band
GROUP BY SalaryBand after creating a column
questions.correct_answer: COUNT(CASE WHEN Salary>=80000 THEN 1 END) for each band
questions.explanation: CASE inside COUNT returns 1 for matches and NULL otherwise; COUNT ignores NULLs.

questions.question_text: Find customers with more than 3 orders — which clause filters the count?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters after GROUP BY aggregation; WHERE cannot reference aggregates.

questions.question_text: A subquery in the FROM clause is called a derived table.
questions.explanation: A subquery used as a table source in FROM is a derived table and must be aliased.

questions.question_text: SELECT * FROM A, B — this produces a:
questions.explanation: Comma-separated tables with no join condition produce a Cartesian product.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you quickly see the columns available in a table when writing a JOIN?
choices: Expand the table in Object Explorer, or type the table alias and press Ctrl+Space for IntelliSense
You must look them up in documentation
questions.correct_answer: Expand the table in Object Explorer, or type the table alias and press Ctrl+Space for IntelliSense
questions.explanation: Object Explorer shows columns under each table; IntelliSense autocompletes after typing the alias and a dot.

questions.question_text: You write: SELECT * FROM Orders o JOIN. What keyboard shortcut triggers IntelliSense to suggest table names?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Space triggers IntelliSense suggestions at the cursor position.

questions.question_text: How do you view the relationships between tables visually in SSMS?
choices: Database Diagrams — right-click Database Diagrams > New Database Diagram
questions.correct_answer: Database Diagrams — right-click Database Diagrams > New Database Diagram
questions.explanation: SSMS Database Diagrams let you view and edit FK relationships visually.

questions.question_text: When a JOIN query returns unexpected duplicate rows, what SSMS feature helps you inspect the data?
choices: Run SELECT DISTINCT first, then use the Results pane to examine
questions.correct_answer: Run SELECT DISTINCT first, then use the Results pane to examine
questions.explanation: Inspect the results grid — look for patterns in duplicated columns to find the JOIN issue.

questions.question_text: How do you copy results from the SSMS Results pane to Excel?
choices: Right-click anywhere in the results grid > Copy With Headers, then paste into Excel
Results cannot be copied to Excel
Ctrl+A then Ctrl+C in the results grid then paste
questions.correct_answer: Right-click anywhere in the results grid > Copy With Headers, then paste into Excel
questions.explanation: 'Copy With Headers' includes column names — essential for pasting into Excel properly.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you save query results directly to a CSV file?
choices: Query > Results To > Results to File (Ctrl+Shift+F) then run the query
Results cannot be saved to file from SSMS
questions.correct_answer: Query > Results To > Results to File (Ctrl+Shift+F) then run the query
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+F switches output mode to file — you'll be prompted for a file name when you run.

questions.question_text: What does the green number in the SSMS status bar at the bottom of the Query Editor show?
choices: Row count of the last query result
questions.correct_answer: Row count of the last query result
questions.explanation: The status bar shows rows returned and execution time after a query completes.

questions.question_text: How do you quickly find all references to a table name across all your open query tabs in SSMS?
choices: Ctrl+F to open Find, search across documents
Object Explorer > Right-click table > View Dependencies
Both Ctrl+F and View Dependencies work for different purposes
questions.correct_answer: Both Ctrl+F and View Dependencies work for different purposes
questions.explanation: Ctrl+F searches text in open editors; View Dependencies shows database-level references.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, what happens if you run a query without selecting a database first?
choices: It fails with 'no database selected' error
It prompts you to choose a database
It uses the last connected database
questions.explanation: If no USE statement or dropdown selection, SSMS defaults to master — table references will fail.

questions.question_text: How do you view the execution time of a query in SSMS?
choices: SET STATISTICS TIME ON before the query, or check the status bar after execution
questions.correct_answer: SET STATISTICS TIME ON before the query, or check the status bar after execution
questions.explanation: Both methods work — status bar shows elapsed time; STATISTICS TIME shows CPU and elapsed time in Messages.

questions.question_text: What SSMS feature lets you compare two result sets side by side?
choices: Open two query tabs, run each, view tabs alternately — SSMS has no built-in side-by-side diff
questions.correct_answer: Open two query tabs, run each, view tabs alternately — SSMS has no built-in side-by-side diff
questions.explanation: SSMS doesn't have a native result diff tool — use Excel or third-party tools for that.

questions.question_text: How do you increase the maximum number of rows returned in SSMS results (default 1000 in some views)?
choices: The Query Editor has no row limit by default — TOP N or WHERE clause limits rows
Tools > Options > Query Results > Max Rows
questions.correct_answer: The Query Editor has no row limit by default — TOP N or WHERE clause limits rows
questions.explanation: The regular Query Editor returns all rows. Limits only apply in the table viewer (Edit Top 200 Rows).

questions.question_text: In SSMS, you can right-click a table in Object Explorer and select 'Select Top 1000 Rows' to instantly preview data.
questions.explanation: This auto-generates and runs a SELECT TOP 1000 query — useful for quick data inspection.

questions.question_text: SSMS IntelliSense works without an active database connection.
questions.explanation: IntelliSense requires a live connection to retrieve metadata about tables, columns and procedures.

questions.question_text: Which query finds duplicate email addresses in the Customers table?
choices: SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT Email FROM Customers WHERE Email IS NOT NULL
SELECT Email FROM Customers ORDER BY Email
questions.correct_answer: SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
questions.explanation: GROUP BY collapses duplicates; HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 exposes them.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between COUNT(*) and COUNT(ColumnName)?
choices: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs; COUNT(col) counts only non-NULL values
questions.correct_answer: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs; COUNT(col) counts only non-NULL values
questions.explanation: COUNT(col) ignores NULLs — useful to measure completeness of a column.

questions.question_text: To find OrderLines where the OrderID does not exist in Orders you use:
choices: LEFT JOIN Orders ON OrderLines.OrderID = Orders.OrderID WHERE Orders.OrderID IS NULL
INNER JOIN Orders ON OrderLines.OrderID = Orders.OrderID
WHERE OrderLines.OrderID NOT IN (SELECT OrderID FROM Orders) -- careful with NULLs
Option A or C (both valid, prefer A for NULL safety)
questions.correct_answer: Option A or C (both valid, prefer A for NULL safety)
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN + IS NULL is the safest pattern; NOT IN works only if OrderID cannot be NULL.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between ISNULL and COALESCE?
choices: ISNULL takes two arguments; COALESCE takes multiple and returns the first non-NULL
questions.correct_answer: ISNULL takes two arguments; COALESCE takes multiple and returns the first non-NULL
questions.explanation: COALESCE is ANSI standard and more flexible; ISNULL is SQL Server specific.

questions.question_text: After loading 50,000 rows, the best single validation query compares:
choices: COUNT(*), SUM, MIN, MAX between source and target in one query
questions.correct_answer: COUNT(*), SUM, MIN, MAX between source and target in one query
questions.explanation: Comparing multiple aggregates at once catches both missing rows and bad transformations.

questions.question_text: IS NULL and = NULL are equivalent in SQL Server.
questions.explanation: = NULL always returns unknown/false; IS NULL is the correct syntax to check for NULLs.

questions.question_text: Which operator returns rows in the first query that do NOT appear in the second?
questions.explanation: EXCEPT returns rows from the first set not present in the second — SQL Server's version of MINUS.

questions.question_text: COALESCE(Phone, Mobile, 'N/A') returns the ___ non-NULL value from the list.
questions.explanation: COALESCE evaluates left to right and returns the first non-NULL it finds.

questions.question_text: A record count reconciliation query uses:
choices: UNION ALL to show source and target counts side by side
INNER JOIN between source and target
questions.correct_answer: UNION ALL to show source and target counts side by side
questions.explanation: UNION ALL stacks source and target counts into one result set for easy comparison.

questions.question_text: An orphaned record is a child row whose parent no longer exists.
questions.explanation: Orphaned records indicate referential integrity violations — child without matching parent.

questions.question_text: Which query flags orders with a suspiciously large or zero/negative amount?
questions.explanation: Range checks catch both zero/negative values and unrealistically large amounts.

questions.question_text: SUM validation between source and target helps detect:
choices: Transformation errors that change values even if row counts match
questions.correct_answer: Transformation errors that change values even if row counts match
questions.explanation: Row counts can match while values differ — SUM catches silent data corruption.

questions.question_text: COALESCE can accept more than two arguments.
questions.explanation: COALESCE accepts any number of arguments and returns the first non-NULL.

questions.question_text: To count NULL values in the Email column you write:
choices: SUM(CASE WHEN Email IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
questions.correct_answer: SUM(CASE WHEN Email IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
questions.explanation: CASE WHEN returns 1 for NULLs; SUM adds them up. COUNT(col) skips NULLs so can't count them directly.

questions.question_text: The EXCEPT operator requires:
choices: The same number and compatible data types in both SELECT lists
A WHERE clause on both sides
questions.correct_answer: The same number and compatible data types in both SELECT lists
questions.explanation: Like UNION, EXCEPT requires matching column count and compatible types.

questions.question_text: When running data validation queries in SSMS, how do you quickly count the total rows returned?
choices: Check the row count in the status bar at the bottom after execution
SELECT COUNT only works in a subquery
questions.correct_answer: Check the row count in the status bar at the bottom after execution
questions.explanation: SSMS shows '(X row(s) affected)' in Messages and row count in the status bar.

questions.question_text: You want to run multiple validation checks in sequence and see all results. What SSMS setting ensures each SELECT shows its own result set?
choices: Results to Grid (default) — each SELECT shows a separate results tab
You can only see the last result set
questions.correct_answer: Results to Grid (default) — each SELECT shows a separate results tab
questions.explanation: In Grid mode, each SELECT statement gets its own tab in the results pane.

questions.question_text: How do you export your data quality validation results to a report in SSMS?
choices: Query > Results To > Results to File, run query, save as .csv or .rpt
questions.correct_answer: Query > Results To > Results to File, run query, save as .csv or .rpt
questions.explanation: Switch to file output mode before running to save results directly to a file.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, what is the quickest way to check if any NULLs exist in a column without writing a query?
choices: Right-click the table > Edit Top 200 Rows and scroll through
Right-click column in Object Explorer > Column Properties — shows nullability but not actual nulls; write a query for counts
NULL counts require a COUNT query — no GUI shortcut
questions.correct_answer: NULL counts require a COUNT query — no GUI shortcut
questions.explanation: Object Explorer shows if NULL is allowed but not how many nulls exist — always write a query.

questions.question_text: You want to validate row counts between a source table and a target table. What SSMS workflow is most efficient?
choices: Open one query tab, write both COUNT queries separated by a semicolon, run with F5 — both result sets appear
questions.correct_answer: Open one query tab, write both COUNT queries separated by a semicolon, run with F5 — both result sets appear
questions.explanation: Multiple SELECT statements in one batch each produce their own result tab.

questions.question_text: How do you format a large validation query for readability in SSMS?
choices: Select the SQL text then press Ctrl+K, Ctrl+F to auto-format
questions.correct_answer: Select the SQL text then press Ctrl+K, Ctrl+F to auto-format
questions.explanation: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+F is SSMS's built-in SQL formatter.

questions.question_text: Where do you write a scheduled validation job that runs automatically every night in SQL Server?
choices: SSMS > SQL Server Agent > Jobs > New Job
SSMS Query Editor with a timer
questions.correct_answer: SSMS > SQL Server Agent > Jobs > New Job
questions.explanation: SQL Server Agent (under Management in Object Explorer) manages scheduled jobs and alerts.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you find which queries are currently running on the server?
choices: Execute sp_who2 or query sys.dm_exec_requests in a new query window
questions.correct_answer: Execute sp_who2 or query sys.dm_exec_requests in a new query window
questions.explanation: Both methods show active sessions — Activity Monitor (Tools menu) provides a GUI alternative.

questions.question_text: How do you comment out a block of validation SQL in SSMS quickly?
choices: Select the lines and press Ctrl+K, Ctrl+C
Type -- before each line manually only
questions.correct_answer: Select the lines and press Ctrl+K, Ctrl+C
questions.explanation: Ctrl+K, Ctrl+C comments selected lines; Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U uncomments them.

questions.question_text: You discover a data issue in production. How do you safely test your fix in SSMS before committing?
choices: Wrap the fix in BEGIN TRAN, test with SELECT, then ROLLBACK if results look wrong before COMMIT
Run it directly — you can always undo with Ctrl+Z
questions.correct_answer: Wrap the fix in BEGIN TRAN, test with SELECT, then ROLLBACK if results look wrong before COMMIT
questions.explanation: BEGIN TRAN lets you preview DML changes; ROLLBACK undoes them safely.

questions.question_text: What SSMS object lets you set up alerts that trigger when a validation threshold is breached (e.g. row count drops to 0)?
choices: SQL Server Agent Alerts under Management in Object Explorer
questions.correct_answer: SQL Server Agent Alerts under Management in Object Explorer
questions.explanation: SQL Server Agent can send email alerts when job steps fail or conditions are met.

questions.question_text: How do you view the history of a SQL Server Agent job (to see if last night's validation passed)?
choices: Right-click the job in SQL Server Agent > Jobs > View History
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the job in SQL Server Agent > Jobs > View History
questions.explanation: View History shows all recent runs, their status, and error messages.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, pressing Ctrl+K then Ctrl+C comments out selected lines. Pressing Ctrl+K then Ctrl+U uncomments them.
questions.explanation: These are the SSMS shortcuts for block comment/uncomment.

questions.question_text: You can run DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) statements inside a BEGIN TRAN block and use ROLLBACK to undo them if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a safe pattern for testing data changes — always wrap destructive DML in a transaction during testing.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
choices: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
questions.correct_answer: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
questions.explanation: WHERE is applied before GROUP BY; HAVING after — only HAVING can reference aggregates.

questions.question_text: ROLLUP(Region, Product) adds which extra rows?
choices: Subtotals per Region and a grand total row
questions.correct_answer: Subtotals per Region and a grand total row
questions.explanation: ROLLUP creates a hierarchy: detail rows, subtotals per first column, then grand total.

questions.question_text: CUBE(Region, Product) differs from ROLLUP because:
choices: CUBE produces subtotals for ALL combinations of columns, not just a hierarchy
CUBE only produces a grand total
questions.correct_answer: CUBE produces subtotals for ALL combinations of columns, not just a hierarchy
questions.explanation: CUBE generates the power set of groupings; ROLLUP generates a hierarchical subset.

questions.question_text: GROUPING(Region) returns 1 when:
choices: The Region column is NULL because it is a summary/total row
Region has a NULL data value
questions.correct_answer: The Region column is NULL because it is a summary/total row
questions.explanation: GROUPING() distinguishes ROLLUP/CUBE NULL (summary) from actual NULL data values.

questions.question_text: GROUPING SETS((Region),(Product),()) is equivalent to:
choices: Three separate GROUP BYs combined with UNION ALL
A single GROUP BY Region, Product
questions.correct_answer: Three separate GROUP BYs combined with UNION ALL
questions.explanation: GROUPING SETS explicitly defines each grouping combination, equivalent to UNION ALL of multiple GROUP BYs.

questions.question_text: You can use an aggregate function in a WHERE clause.
questions.explanation: Aggregates cannot appear in WHERE; use HAVING instead.

questions.question_text: Which aggregate ignores NULL values?
choices: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT(col) — all ignore NULLs except COUNT(*)
questions.correct_answer: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT(col) — all ignore NULLs except COUNT(*)
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts all rows; all other aggregates and COUNT(col) skip NULLs.

questions.question_text: GROUP BY ___ adds subtotals and a grand total to a query.
questions.explanation: ROLLUP extends GROUP BY with hierarchical subtotals.

questions.question_text: SELECT Region, SUM(Sales) FROM Orders GROUP BY ROLLUP(Region) — the grand total row has Region =
questions.explanation: ROLLUP uses NULL to mark summary rows; use GROUPING() to identify them.

questions.question_text: GROUPING SETS give more flexibility than ROLLUP when you need custom grouping combinations.
questions.explanation: GROUPING SETS lets you define exactly which combinations you want, unlike ROLLUP's fixed hierarchy.

questions.question_text: AVG(Salary) vs SUM(Salary)/COUNT(*) differ when:
choices: Salary contains NULLs — AVG ignores NULLs but COUNT(*) includes all rows
questions.correct_answer: Salary contains NULLs — AVG ignores NULLs but COUNT(*) includes all rows
questions.explanation: AVG skips NULLs in both numerator and denominator; SUM/COUNT(*) includes NULL rows in denominator.

questions.question_text: To show total sales per region with a grand total in ONE query you use:
choices: GROUP BY Region UNION SELECT NULL, SUM(Sales)
questions.explanation: ROLLUP on a single column adds just the grand total row.

questions.question_text: CUBE(A,B) and ROLLUP(A,B) always produce the same number of rows.
questions.explanation: CUBE produces more rows — it generates all possible grouping combinations including (B) alone.

questions.question_text: To filter groups where total sales exceed 10000 after GROUP BY:
questions.explanation: HAVING filters after aggregation — the only way to filter on aggregates.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly combines a WHERE and HAVING?
choices: SELECT Dept, AVG(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE Active=1 GROUP BY Dept HAVING AVG(Salary)>60000
SELECT Dept, AVG(Salary) FROM Employees HAVING AVG(Salary)>60000 WHERE Active=1 GROUP BY Dept
SELECT Dept, AVG(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE Active=1 AND AVG(Salary)>60000 GROUP BY Dept
SELECT Dept, AVG(Salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY Dept WHERE Active=1 HAVING AVG(Salary)>60000
questions.correct_answer: SELECT Dept, AVG(Salary) FROM Employees WHERE Active=1 GROUP BY Dept HAVING AVG(Salary)>60000
questions.explanation: Correct clause order: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → ORDER BY.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, when a GROUP BY query returns an error 'Column is invalid in select list because it is not contained in GROUP BY', what does this mean?
choices: You need to add ORDER BY
Every column in SELECT must either appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate function
questions.correct_answer: Every column in SELECT must either appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate function
questions.explanation: This is the fundamental GROUP BY rule — non-aggregated columns must be in GROUP BY.

questions.question_text: How do you view aggregated query results in a chart inside SSMS?
choices: SSMS has no chart feature — export to Excel or Power BI for visualisation
questions.correct_answer: SSMS has no chart feature — export to Excel or Power BI for visualisation
questions.explanation: SSMS is a query tool — visualisation is done in reporting tools like Power BI or Excel.

questions.question_text: You want to verify ROLLUP is working correctly. How do you identify the grand total row in the result set?
choices: It is always the first row
It has NULL in the grouping columns — use GROUPING() = 1 to confirm
ROLLUP adds a column called GrandTotal
questions.correct_answer: It has NULL in the grouping columns — use GROUPING() = 1 to confirm
questions.explanation: ROLLUP uses NULL to represent subtotal/grand total rows — GROUPING() returns 1 for those NULLs.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you quickly rerun the last executed query?
choices: Press F5 again — the last query text stays in the editor
questions.correct_answer: Press F5 again — the last query text stays in the editor
questions.explanation: The query text remains in the editor tab — just press F5 to re-execute it.

questions.question_text: How do you pin a frequently used aggregation query so it's easy to find in SSMS?
choices: Save it as a .sql file (Ctrl+S) and organise in a folder, or add to a registered query in SSMS
SSMS has a Favourites panel for queries
questions.correct_answer: Save it as a .sql file (Ctrl+S) and organise in a folder, or add to a registered query in SSMS
questions.explanation: There's no built-in favourites — saving .sql files to organised folders is the standard practice.

questions.question_text: What happens in SSMS if you include a column in SELECT but forget to add it to GROUP BY?
choices: SSMS auto-adds it to GROUP BY
An error: 'Column is invalid in the select list'
The query runs but ignores that column
NULL is returned for that column
questions.correct_answer: An error: 'Column is invalid in the select list'
questions.explanation: SQL Server enforces strict GROUP BY rules — missing columns cause an immediate error.

questions.question_text: You run a ROLLUP query and see unexpected NULL values in your dimension columns. What SSMS feature helps you confirm this is ROLLUP behaviour, not bad data?
choices: Add GROUPING(col) to your SELECT — it returns 1 for rollup-generated NULLs and 0 for real data NULLs
Filter WHERE col IS NOT NULL
questions.correct_answer: Add GROUPING(col) to your SELECT — it returns 1 for rollup-generated NULLs and 0 for real data NULLs
questions.explanation: GROUPING() distinguishes between actual NULL data and rollup summary rows.

questions.question_text: How do you export aggregated SSMS results to a format business users can read?
choices: Right-click results > Copy With Headers, paste into Excel; or use Results to File to save as CSV
questions.correct_answer: Right-click results > Copy With Headers, paste into Excel; or use Results to File to save as CSV
questions.explanation: Copy With Headers or Results to File are the two main export paths from SSMS.

questions.question_text: What SSMS shortcut selects all text in the Query Editor?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+A selects all text in the active editor window.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you find the query that's consuming the most CPU on the server right now?
choices: Query sys.dm_exec_query_stats ordered by total_worker_time DESC
sp_who2 shows CPU usage per query
questions.correct_answer: Query sys.dm_exec_query_stats ordered by total_worker_time DESC
questions.explanation: This DMV stores cached query plans and their cumulative resource usage — sort by CPU or reads to find expensive queries.

questions.question_text: How do you add line numbers to the SSMS Query Editor for easier reference?
choices: Tools > Options > Text Editor > Transact-SQL > General > Line Numbers (check the box)
questions.correct_answer: Tools > Options > Text Editor > Transact-SQL > General > Line Numbers (check the box)
questions.explanation: This setting persists across sessions once enabled.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, what does the 'Results to Text' output mode show differently from 'Results to Grid'?
choices: Results to Text shows output as plain text columns separated by spaces — easier to copy as text
Results to Text shows execution plans
Results to Text shows XML output only
questions.correct_answer: Results to Text shows output as plain text columns separated by spaces — easier to copy as text
questions.explanation: Text mode (Ctrl+T) is useful for simple outputs; Grid mode (Ctrl+D) is better for wide result sets.

questions.question_text: Ctrl+T in SSMS switches the query results to Text mode, and Ctrl+D switches back to Grid mode.
questions.explanation: These shortcuts toggle result output format between text and grid.

questions.question_text: HAVING can filter on a column that does not appear in the SELECT list.
questions.explanation: HAVING filters based on aggregate expressions — the column doesn't need to be in SELECT.

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between OLTP and OLAP?
choices: OLTP handles transactional row-level operations; OLAP handles analytical aggregations
OLTP is read-only; OLAP allows writes
OLAP is normalised; OLTP is denormalised
questions.correct_answer: OLTP handles transactional row-level operations; OLAP handles analytical aggregations
questions.explanation: OLTP optimises for fast writes; OLAP optimises for fast reads across large datasets.

questions.question_text: A Fact Table contains:
choices: Measurable business events with numeric measures and foreign keys to dimensions
Descriptive attributes like customer name and product category
questions.correct_answer: Measurable business events with numeric measures and foreign keys to dimensions
questions.explanation: Fact tables store the 'what happened' — sales amounts, quantities, counts.

questions.question_text: Star Schema vs Snowflake Schema — the key difference is:
choices: Star has denormalised dimensions connected directly to the fact; Snowflake normalises dimensions into sub-tables
Star is normalised; Snowflake is not
questions.correct_answer: Star has denormalised dimensions connected directly to the fact; Snowflake normalises dimensions into sub-tables
questions.explanation: Star is simpler and faster to query; Snowflake saves storage but adds join complexity.

questions.question_text: SCD Type 2 handles historical changes by:
choices: Adding a new row with effective dates and an IsCurrent flag
questions.correct_answer: Adding a new row with effective dates and an IsCurrent flag
questions.explanation: Type 2 preserves full history — each change creates a new row with date range tracking.

questions.question_text: ETL vs ELT — ELT is preferred in cloud data warehouses because:
choices: Raw data is loaded first and transformed inside the warehouse using its compute power
ETL is faster in the cloud
ELT does not require a staging area
questions.correct_answer: Raw data is loaded first and transformed inside the warehouse using its compute power
questions.explanation: Cloud warehouses like Synapse and Snowflake have massive compute — ELT leverages this.

questions.question_text: A Dimension table contains the measurable facts like sales amounts.
questions.explanation: Dimension tables contain descriptive attributes; Fact tables contain measures.

questions.question_text: Which SCD type simply overwrites the old value with no history?
questions.explanation: SCD Type 1 overwrites — simplest but loses historical data.

questions.question_text: A Date dimension is important in a data warehouse because:
choices: It allows filtering and grouping by year, quarter, month, week, day — enabling time intelligence
questions.correct_answer: It allows filtering and grouping by year, quarter, month, week, day — enabling time intelligence
questions.explanation: A pre-built Date dimension enables rich time-based analysis without complex date functions.

questions.question_text: In a Star Schema, dimension tables connect directly to the ___ table.
questions.explanation: The fact table is at the centre; dimensions radiate outward like star points.

questions.question_text: Snowflake Schema always performs better than Star Schema for queries.
questions.explanation: Star Schema typically performs better for queries due to fewer joins; Snowflake saves storage.

questions.question_text: The staging area in an ETL pipeline is used to:
choices: Hold raw source data temporarily before transformation and loading
questions.correct_answer: Hold raw source data temporarily before transformation and loading
questions.explanation: Staging decouples extraction from transformation, enabling restarts and auditing.

questions.question_text: SCD Type 3 stores:
choices: Only the current and one previous value in separate columns
questions.correct_answer: Only the current and one previous value in separate columns
questions.explanation: Type 3 adds a 'Previous Value' column — simple but limited to one historical state.

questions.question_text: A Fact table typically has more rows than a Dimension table.
questions.explanation: Facts record every business event (millions of sales); Dimensions describe entities (thousands of customers).

questions.question_text: Grain of a fact table refers to:
choices: The level of detail each row represents — e.g. one row per transaction
questions.correct_answer: The level of detail each row represents — e.g. one row per transaction
questions.explanation: Defining the grain first ensures consistency — all facts must be at the same level of detail.

questions.question_text: Which schema type is generally recommended for Power BI performance?
questions.explanation: Power BI and most BI tools perform best with a simple Star Schema.

questions.question_text: Which Microsoft tool is commonly used to design and deploy Data Warehouse schemas visually?
choices: SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) in Visual Studio
questions.correct_answer: SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) in Visual Studio
questions.explanation: SSDT provides database project templates for designing, deploying and versioning DW schemas.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, how do you create a new table for a fact table in your data warehouse?
choices: Right-click Tables > New Table — opens table designer OR write CREATE TABLE in Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Right-click Tables > New Table — opens table designer OR write CREATE TABLE in Query Editor
questions.explanation: Both the GUI table designer and T-SQL CREATE TABLE work.

questions.question_text: How do you view the relationships (foreign keys) between fact and dimension tables in SSMS?
choices: Database Diagrams — right-click > New Database Diagram and add the relevant tables
questions.correct_answer: Database Diagrams — right-click > New Database Diagram and add the relevant tables
questions.explanation: Database Diagrams show FK relationships visually — drag tables in, lines show relationships.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, where do you find an existing SCD Type 2 stored procedure for managing dimension updates?
questions.explanation: All stored procedures including SCD logic live under Programmability > Stored Procedures.

questions.question_text: How do you bulk load data into a fact table efficiently in SQL Server?
choices: BULK INSERT statement or SSIS OLE DB Destination with Fast Load option
INSERT one row at a time
Right-click table > Import Data wizard in SSMS
questions.correct_answer: BULK INSERT statement or SSIS OLE DB Destination with Fast Load option
questions.explanation: BULK INSERT and SSIS Fast Load use minimally-logged operations for high performance.

questions.question_text: How do you check the size of your fact table and how much disk space it's using in SSMS?
choices: Right-click the table > Properties > Storage tab shows row count and disk usage
SELECT COUNT(*) only shows rows, not size
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the table > Properties > Storage tab shows row count and disk usage
questions.explanation: Table Properties > Storage shows reserved, data, index, and unused space.

questions.question_text: In a data warehouse, how do you enforce that a surrogate key column auto-increments in SQL Server?
choices: Define the column as IDENTITY(1,1) in the CREATE TABLE statement
questions.correct_answer: Define the column as IDENTITY(1,1) in the CREATE TABLE statement
questions.explanation: IDENTITY(seed, increment) auto-generates surrogate key values — no application code needed.

questions.question_text: How do you implement an SCD Type 2 update using SSMS? Which statement handles both the expire of the old row and insert of the new row atomically?
choices: MERGE statement with WHEN MATCHED UPDATE (set ExpiryDate) and WHEN NOT MATCHED INSERT
Two separate UPDATE and INSERT inside a BEGIN TRAN
A stored procedure is the only way
questions.correct_answer: MERGE statement with WHEN MATCHED UPDATE (set ExpiryDate) and WHEN NOT MATCHED INSERT
questions.explanation: MERGE handles upsert logic in one atomic statement — ideal for SCD Type 2.

questions.question_text: Where in SSMS do you monitor an ETL job that loads the data warehouse overnight?
choices: Management > SQL Server Agent > Jobs — right-click > View History
questions.correct_answer: Management > SQL Server Agent > Jobs — right-click > View History
questions.explanation: SQL Server Agent manages scheduled ETL jobs; View History shows success/failure.

questions.question_text: How do you add an index to a dimension table in SSMS to improve JOIN performance?
choices: Right-click the table > Design > Indexes/Keys tab, or use CREATE INDEX in Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the table > Design > Indexes/Keys tab, or use CREATE INDEX in Query Editor
questions.explanation: Both the GUI designer and T-SQL CREATE INDEX statement work for adding indexes.

questions.question_text: What SSMS report shows database growth over time for capacity planning your data warehouse?
choices: Right-click the database > Reports > Standard Reports > Disk Usage by Table
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the database > Reports > Standard Reports > Disk Usage by Table
questions.explanation: Standard Reports include pre-built disk usage, index usage, and performance reports.

questions.question_text: How do you partition a large fact table in SQL Server to improve query performance?
choices: Create a Partition Function, Partition Scheme, then CREATE TABLE ON the scheme — all done via T-SQL in Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Create a Partition Function, Partition Scheme, then CREATE TABLE ON the scheme — all done via T-SQL in Query Editor
questions.explanation: Table partitioning requires T-SQL DDL — SSMS has a Partition Wizard too (right-click table > Storage > Manage Partition).

questions.question_text: In SSMS, you can right-click a database and click 'Reports > Standard Reports' to see pre-built performance and disk usage dashboards.
questions.explanation: Standard Reports are built-in SSMS reports for quick server and database health checks.

questions.question_text: A CLUSTERED index on a fact table should always be on the surrogate key column for best performance.
questions.explanation: Fact tables are often clustered on date key or a composite of common filter columns — surrogate key is usually a non-clustered PK.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Control Flow and Data Flow in SSIS?
choices: Control Flow orchestrates task execution order; Data Flow moves and transforms data
questions.correct_answer: Control Flow orchestrates task execution order; Data Flow moves and transforms data
questions.explanation: Control Flow is the workflow engine; Data Flow is the ETL pipeline inside it.

questions.question_text: The Execute SQL Task is used to:
choices: Run T-SQL statements — truncate tables, call stored procedures, insert log records
questions.correct_answer: Run T-SQL statements — truncate tables, call stored procedures, insert log records
questions.explanation: Execute SQL Task runs any T-SQL against a database connection.

questions.question_text: Precedence Constraints connect tasks with logic such as:
choices: Success, Failure, or Completion — controlling which path executes next
They have no logic — they are just connectors
questions.correct_answer: Success, Failure, or Completion — controlling which path executes next
questions.explanation: Precedence Constraints define the conditional flow between tasks.

questions.question_text: A Script Task in SSIS allows you to:
choices: Write custom C# or VB.NET code for logic not available in built-in tasks
questions.correct_answer: Write custom C# or VB.NET code for logic not available in built-in tasks
questions.explanation: Script Task gives full .NET flexibility for complex custom logic.

questions.question_text: SSIS Variables are used to:
choices: Store dynamic values at runtime — passed between tasks or used in expressions
questions.correct_answer: Store dynamic values at runtime — passed between tasks or used in expressions
questions.explanation: Variables enable dynamic behaviour — file names, row counts, flags between tasks.

questions.question_text: A Foreach Loop Container iterates over a recordset or file collection.
questions.explanation: Foreach Loop is used to process multiple files, rows, or ADO recordsets in a loop.

questions.question_text: Which SSIS task would you use to copy a file from one folder to another?
questions.explanation: File System Task handles file operations: copy, move, rename, delete.

questions.question_text: An SSIS Event Handler (e.g. OnError) is used to:
choices: Run logic when a specific event occurs — e.g. send email on task failure
questions.correct_answer: Run logic when a specific event occurs — e.g. send email on task failure
questions.explanation: Event Handlers provide error trapping and notification at the package or task level.

questions.question_text: In SSIS, the ___ task runs T-SQL against a database connection.
questions.explanation: Execute SQL Task is the standard way to run SQL statements in Control Flow.

questions.question_text: Precedence Constraints can evaluate both expression AND constraint (Success/Failure) together.
questions.explanation: You can combine Success/Failure logic with an expression for fine-grained flow control.

questions.question_text: Package-level variables in SSIS are accessible:
choices: Across all tasks and containers within the package
Only in the task that created them
questions.correct_answer: Across all tasks and containers within the package
questions.explanation: Package-scope variables are visible everywhere in that package.

questions.question_text: The SSIS Catalog (SSISDB) is used for:
choices: Deploying, executing, monitoring and logging SSIS packages
questions.correct_answer: Deploying, executing, monitoring and logging SSIS packages
questions.explanation: SSISDB is the deployment and operations repository for SSIS in SQL Server.

questions.question_text: A Script Task can read and write SSIS package variables.
questions.explanation: Script Task can read/write Dts.Variables — enabling dynamic logic based on runtime values.

questions.question_text: Which container runs a set of tasks repeatedly for each item in a collection?
questions.explanation: Foreach Loop iterates over collections; For Loop iterates a fixed number of times.

questions.question_text: To run an SSIS package on a schedule, you use:
questions.explanation: SQL Agent integrates with SSISDB to schedule and run packages.

questions.question_text: Which application do you use to build SSIS packages?
choices: SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) inside Visual Studio
questions.correct_answer: SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) inside Visual Studio
questions.explanation: SSIS packages are built in SSDT/Visual Studio using the Integration Services Project template.

questions.question_text: How do you create a new SSIS project?
choices: Visual Studio > File > New > Project > Integration Services Project
questions.correct_answer: Visual Studio > File > New > Project > Integration Services Project
questions.explanation: Select the Business Intelligence or SQL Server category in VS's new project dialog.

questions.question_text: In the SSIS designer, what are the two main design surfaces you switch between?
choices: Control Flow tab and Data Flow tab
questions.correct_answer: Control Flow tab and Data Flow tab
questions.explanation: Control Flow orchestrates tasks; Data Flow handles column-level transformations — they are separate tabs.

questions.question_text: How do you add a new task to the Control Flow in SSIS?
choices: Drag from the SSIS Toolbox on the left onto the Control Flow design surface
questions.correct_answer: Drag from the SSIS Toolbox on the left onto the Control Flow design surface
questions.explanation: The SSIS Toolbox panel contains all available tasks — drag them onto the canvas.

questions.question_text: How do you connect two tasks in the SSIS Control Flow with a Precedence Constraint?
choices: Hover over the source task until a green arrow appears, then drag it to the next task
Draw a line with the Line tool
Tasks auto-connect when placed near each other
questions.correct_answer: Hover over the source task until a green arrow appears, then drag it to the next task
questions.explanation: The green arrow is the success constraint; you can change it to failure or completion by double-clicking.

questions.question_text: How do you configure a Precedence Constraint to run the next task ONLY if the previous one succeeded?
choices: Double-click the constraint arrow > Evaluation Operation = Constraint > Value = Success
It defaults to Success — no change needed
questions.correct_answer: Double-click the constraint arrow > Evaluation Operation = Constraint > Value = Success
questions.explanation: Double-clicking the arrow opens the Precedence Constraint Editor — Success is the default but you can change to Failure or Completion.

questions.question_text: Where do you define a package-level SSIS variable?
choices: SSIS menu > Variables — opens the Variables panel
questions.correct_answer: SSIS menu > Variables — opens the Variables panel
questions.explanation: The Variables panel (SSIS menu > Variables) is where you define, name, and set scope for variables.

questions.question_text: How do you run/test an SSIS package directly from Visual Studio without deploying it?
choices: Press F5 or Debug > Start Debugging — runs the package in debug mode
You must deploy first before running
questions.correct_answer: Press F5 or Debug > Start Debugging — runs the package in debug mode
questions.explanation: F5 runs the package in the VS debugger — tasks turn green (success) or red (failure) as they execute.

questions.question_text: What colour does an SSIS task turn when it executes successfully in debug mode?
questions.explanation: Green = success, Red = failure, Yellow = running, Grey = not yet run.

questions.question_text: How do you deploy an SSIS package to the SSIS Catalog on SQL Server?
choices: Right-click the project in Solution Explorer > Deploy — follow the Integration Services Deployment Wizard
Copy the file to the SQL Server folder
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the project in Solution Explorer > Deploy — follow the Integration Services Deployment Wizard
questions.explanation: The wizard deploys to the SSISDB catalog on the target SQL Server.

questions.question_text: Where do you view SSIS package execution logs in SSMS after deployment?
choices: Integration Services Catalogs > SSISDB > your folder > right-click execution > All Executions
questions.correct_answer: Integration Services Catalogs > SSISDB > your folder > right-click execution > All Executions
questions.explanation: The SSIS Catalog in SSMS records all executions with detailed logging.

questions.question_text: How do you add error handling to an SSIS Control Flow task?
choices: Right-click the task > Edit > Error Output tab, OR add an Event Handler in the Event Handlers tab
Add a Try/Catch task from the toolbox
Error handling is not possible in SSIS
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the task > Edit > Error Output tab, OR add an Event Handler in the Event Handlers tab
questions.explanation: Event Handlers (separate tab) handle OnError, OnTaskFailed events at the package or task level.

questions.question_text: When an SSIS task fails in debug mode in Visual Studio, it turns red.
questions.explanation: Red indicates failure; the Output window shows the error message.

questions.question_text: SSIS package variables set at package scope are visible to all tasks within that package.
questions.explanation: Package-scoped variables are accessible by all tasks and containers in the package.

questions.question_text: The Lookup transformation in SSIS is used to:
choices: Join a streaming dataset to a reference dataset to enrich or validate rows
questions.correct_answer: Join a streaming dataset to a reference dataset to enrich or validate rows
questions.explanation: Lookup matches rows from the pipeline against a reference table, like a JOIN.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Merge and Union All in SSIS?
choices: Merge requires both inputs to be sorted; Union All does not require sorting
questions.correct_answer: Merge requires both inputs to be sorted; Union All does not require sorting
questions.explanation: Merge is like a sorted union; Union All simply stacks inputs with no sort requirement.

questions.question_text: The Conditional Split transformation routes rows based on:
choices: Conditions/expressions — like a CASE WHEN for directing rows to different outputs
questions.correct_answer: Conditions/expressions — like a CASE WHEN for directing rows to different outputs
questions.explanation: Conditional Split evaluates conditions in order and sends rows to the first matching output.

questions.question_text: Lookup cache modes in SSIS are:
choices: Full Cache (load all at start), Partial Cache, No Cache
questions.correct_answer: Full Cache (load all at start), Partial Cache, No Cache
questions.explanation: Full Cache is fastest for small-medium reference tables; No Cache queries per row (slowest).

questions.question_text: A Derived Column transformation is used to:
choices: Create new columns or replace existing ones using expressions — like a calculated column
questions.correct_answer: Create new columns or replace existing ones using expressions — like a calculated column
questions.explanation: Derived Column applies SSIS expressions to create or modify columns in the pipeline.

questions.question_text: OLE DB Source can read data using an inline SQL query.
questions.explanation: OLE DB Source supports Table, View, or SQL Command as data access modes.

questions.question_text: Merge Join in SSIS is equivalent to which SQL operation?
choices: SQL JOIN (INNER, LEFT, FULL) but requires sorted inputs
questions.correct_answer: SQL JOIN (INNER, LEFT, FULL) but requires sorted inputs
questions.explanation: Merge Join performs JOIN operations in the data flow, requiring both inputs to be sorted.

questions.question_text: The ___ transformation adds new calculated columns to the data flow pipeline.
questions.explanation: Derived Column uses SSIS expressions to create or modify columns.

questions.question_text: When a Lookup finds no match, the row goes to:
choices: The No Match output — which you can redirect to handle errors or log misses
questions.correct_answer: The No Match output — which you can redirect to handle errors or log misses
questions.explanation: Redirecting no-match rows to a separate output allows graceful handling of unmatched data.

questions.question_text: The Aggregate transformation in SSIS performs GROUP BY operations in the data flow.
questions.explanation: Aggregate applies SUM, COUNT, AVG, GROUP BY within the pipeline before the destination.

questions.question_text: OLE DB Destination with Fast Load mode uses:
choices: Bulk insert for high performance — similar to BULK INSERT or bcp
questions.correct_answer: Bulk insert for high performance — similar to BULK INSERT or bcp
questions.explanation: Fast Load uses the bulk copy API, dramatically improving load performance.

questions.question_text: To send UK customers to one table and US customers to another in one Data Flow:
choices: Use Conditional Split with country conditions, then two OLE DB Destinations
Use two separate Data Flow Tasks
questions.correct_answer: Use Conditional Split with country conditions, then two OLE DB Destinations
questions.explanation: Conditional Split routes rows to different outputs in a single pass.

questions.question_text: Merge Join in SSIS requires both input streams to be sorted on the join key.
questions.explanation: Unlike SQL JOIN, SSIS Merge Join requires pre-sorted inputs — use Sort transformation first.

questions.question_text: A Flat File Source in SSIS reads from:
choices: CSV, delimited, fixed-width, or ragged-right text files
questions.correct_answer: CSV, delimited, fixed-width, or ragged-right text files
questions.explanation: Flat File Source handles common text file formats through a Flat File Connection Manager.

questions.question_text: To remove exact duplicate rows in a SSIS Data Flow you use:
choices: Sort transformation with Remove Duplicate Rows option checked
questions.correct_answer: Sort transformation with Remove Duplicate Rows option checked
questions.explanation: The Sort transformation has a built-in option to eliminate duplicate rows.

questions.question_text: To access the Data Flow design surface in SSIS, what do you do first?
choices: Double-click a Data Flow Task in the Control Flow
Click the Data Flow tab at the top of the designer
Both — double-clicking opens the Data Flow for that specific task; the tab switches to it
questions.correct_answer: Both — double-clicking opens the Data Flow for that specific task; the tab switches to it
questions.explanation: Double-clicking the Data Flow Task on the Control Flow canvas opens that task's Data Flow in the Data Flow tab.

questions.question_text: How do you add an OLE DB Source to read from SQL Server in the Data Flow?
choices: Drag 'OLE DB Source' from the SSIS Toolbox onto the Data Flow canvas
Right-click canvas > Add Source > OLE DB
questions.correct_answer: Drag 'OLE DB Source' from the SSIS Toolbox onto the Data Flow canvas
questions.explanation: All Data Flow components are in the SSIS Toolbox under 'Data Flow Sources'.

questions.question_text: How do you connect a Source component to a Transformation in the Data Flow?
choices: Drag the blue output arrow from the source to the transformation component
Draw a line between them with the connector tool
questions.correct_answer: Drag the blue output arrow from the source to the transformation component
questions.explanation: Blue arrows are data flow paths; red arrows are error outputs.

questions.question_text: How do you configure a Lookup transformation to match on a specific column?
choices: Double-click the Lookup > Connection tab (set the reference table) > Columns tab (drag source column to lookup column to define the join)
questions.correct_answer: Double-click the Lookup > Connection tab (set the reference table) > Columns tab (drag source column to lookup column to define the join)
questions.explanation: The Lookup editor has tabs: General (cache mode), Connection (reference), Columns (mappings), Advanced.

questions.question_text: In SSIS Data Flow, the red arrow from a component represents what?
choices: A failure path — rows that don't match (e.g. Lookup no-match) or error rows are routed here
questions.correct_answer: A failure path — rows that don't match (e.g. Lookup no-match) or error rows are routed here
questions.explanation: Red arrows route error/no-match rows to an error handler or another destination.

questions.question_text: How do you see how many rows are flowing through a Data Flow path during debug execution?
choices: Row counts appear on each connector arrow during execution in debug mode
You must add a Row Count transformation
questions.correct_answer: Row counts appear on each connector arrow during execution in debug mode
questions.explanation: During F5 debug, SSIS displays live row counts on each blue arrow between components.

questions.question_text: How do you create a new derived column in SSIS Data Flow to concatenate FirstName and LastName?
choices: Add a Derived Column transformation, double-click it, define the new column with expression [FirstName] + ' ' + [LastName]
Add it in the source SQL query
questions.correct_answer: Add a Derived Column transformation, double-click it, define the new column with expression [FirstName] + ' ' + [LastName]
questions.explanation: The Derived Column editor lets you define expressions using available input columns.

questions.question_text: How do you configure an OLE DB Destination to use Fast Load (bulk insert) mode for better performance?
choices: Double-click the OLE DB Destination > Component Properties tab > FastLoadOptions or check 'Table or View - Fast Load' in Access Mode
It defaults to Fast Load automatically
questions.correct_answer: Double-click the OLE DB Destination > Component Properties tab > FastLoadOptions or check 'Table or View - Fast Load' in Access Mode
questions.explanation: Fast Load uses bulk insert operations — significantly faster than row-by-row insert.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Merge and Union All in the SSIS Data Flow toolbox?
choices: Merge requires both inputs to be SORTED on the same columns; Union All has no sort requirement
Merge is faster because it is parallel
Union All removes duplicates; Merge keeps them
questions.correct_answer: Merge requires both inputs to be SORTED on the same columns; Union All has no sort requirement
questions.explanation: Merge is like a SQL UNION but requires sorted inputs. Union All is simpler and more common.

questions.question_text: How do you handle rows that fail the Lookup (no match found) in SSIS?
choices: Connect the red no-match output arrow to a separate destination (e.g. flat file or error table) to capture them
Set Lookup to Ignore Failure — all rows pass through
questions.correct_answer: Connect the red no-match output arrow to a separate destination (e.g. flat file or error table) to capture them
questions.explanation: Always route the no-match output — dropping unknown rows silently causes data loss.

questions.question_text: Where do you set the Conditional Split conditions in SSIS?
choices: Double-click the Conditional Split transformation > enter condition expressions and output names for each route
questions.correct_answer: Double-click the Conditional Split transformation > enter condition expressions and output names for each route
questions.explanation: The editor shows rows of conditions — each becomes a named output arrow.

questions.question_text: How do you save and build an SSIS project before deploying it?
choices: Ctrl+Shift+B (Build Solution) — checks for errors before deployment
questions.correct_answer: Ctrl+Shift+B (Build Solution) — checks for errors before deployment
questions.explanation: Always build (Ctrl+Shift+B) to catch configuration errors before deploying to the server.

questions.question_text: In SSIS Data Flow, each component must be connected — an unconnected component causes a validation error.
questions.explanation: All Data Flow components must have connected input/output paths — orphaned components block execution.

questions.question_text: The Aggregate transformation in SSIS Data Flow can perform GROUP BY, SUM, COUNT, and AVG operations before writing to the destination.
questions.explanation: The Aggregate component mirrors SQL GROUP BY logic within the data pipeline.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a Measure and a Calculated Column in Power BI?
choices: Measure aggregates at query time (not stored); Calculated Column is computed row-by-row at refresh (stored)
questions.correct_answer: Measure aggregates at query time (not stored); Calculated Column is computed row-by-row at refresh (stored)
questions.explanation: Measures are virtual and context-aware; Calculated Columns add a physical column to the table.

questions.question_text: What does CALCULATE() do in DAX?
choices: Evaluates an expression in a modified filter context
questions.correct_answer: Evaluates an expression in a modified filter context
questions.explanation: CALCULATE is the most important DAX function — it changes the filter context for an expression.

questions.question_text: ALL() in DAX is used to:
choices: Remove filters from a column or table — enabling % of total calculations
questions.correct_answer: Remove filters from a column or table — enabling % of total calculations
questions.explanation: ALL() clears filters so the denominator in % calculations sees the full dataset.

questions.question_text: RELATED() in DAX is used in a Calculated Column to:
choices: Fetch a value from a related table in the many-to-one direction
questions.correct_answer: Fetch a value from a related table in the many-to-one direction
questions.explanation: RELATED traverses the relationship to get a column value from the related (one-side) table.

questions.question_text: To calculate Year-to-Date sales in DAX:
questions.explanation: DATESYTD returns a date table from Jan 1 to the current date; CALCULATE applies it as a filter.

questions.question_text: In Power BI, relationships should be set up in the Data Model before writing DAX measures.
questions.explanation: DAX functions like RELATED and CALCULATE rely on correct model relationships.

questions.question_text: ALLEXCEPT(Table, Column) removes all filters EXCEPT:
choices: The specified column — useful for subtotals that preserve one filter
questions.correct_answer: The specified column — useful for subtotals that preserve one filter
questions.explanation: ALLEXCEPT clears all filters on the table except those on the listed columns.

questions.question_text: The DAX function that compares the same period last year is ___.
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the date context back exactly one year.

questions.question_text: A one-to-many relationship in Power BI means:
choices: One row in the dimension matches many rows in the fact table
questions.correct_answer: One row in the dimension matches many rows in the fact table
questions.explanation: Standard star schema relationship: one Customer to many Sales rows.

questions.question_text: CALCULATE can accept multiple filter arguments.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE(expression, filter1, filter2, ...) — all filters are applied simultaneously.

questions.question_text: Cross-filter direction in Power BI relationships controls:
choices: Which direction filters propagate between tables
questions.correct_answer: Which direction filters propagate between tables
questions.explanation: Single direction: filter flows one way. Both directions: filters flow both ways (use carefully).

questions.question_text: To % of total sales by region: Total Sales / ___ Total Sales
questions.explanation: ALL(Sales) removes all filters so the denominator is the grand total.

questions.question_text: A calculated column in Power BI can use CALCULATE.
questions.explanation: CALCULATE can be used in calculated columns, but context differs from measures.

questions.question_text: DATESYTD() requires a:
choices: Calendar/Date table with a continuous date column marked as a date table
questions.correct_answer: Calendar/Date table with a continuous date column marked as a date table
questions.explanation: Time intelligence functions in DAX require a proper date table marked in the model.

questions.question_text: The main advantage of a Star Schema in Power BI is:
choices: Fewer joins, simpler DAX, and better query performance
questions.correct_answer: Fewer joins, simpler DAX, and better query performance
questions.explanation: Power BI's Vertipaq engine is optimised for Star Schema — fewer relationships = faster queries.

questions.question_text: Which application do you open to write and run T-SQL window functions against SQL Server?
questions.explanation: SSMS is the primary IDE for SQL Server T-SQL development.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, where do you type your SQL query?
questions.explanation: The Query Editor is the central text area where you write T-SQL.

questions.question_text: What keyboard shortcut executes a query in SSMS?
questions.explanation: F5 (or clicking Execute) runs the selected or entire query in SSMS.

questions.question_text: How do you open a new query window in SSMS?
choices: File > New > Query with Current Connection
Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
questions.correct_answer: Both Ctrl+N and the toolbar New Query button
questions.explanation: Both methods open a fresh query editor tab connected to the current server.

questions.question_text: Where do you see query results after pressing F5 in SSMS?
choices: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
questions.correct_answer: Results pane at the bottom of the Query Editor
questions.explanation: Results appear in the bottom pane; the Messages tab shows row counts and errors.

questions.question_text: To switch to a different database inside SSMS, what are your two options?
choices: Only the database dropdown at the top toolbar
USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
questions.correct_answer: USE DatabaseName in T-SQL OR the database dropdown in the toolbar
questions.explanation: Both methods work — the dropdown is quicker for ad hoc work.

questions.question_text: Where do you find existing stored procedures for a database in SSMS Object Explorer?
questions.explanation: Expand your database node, then Programmability, then Stored Procedures.

questions.question_text: How do you view and edit an existing stored procedure in SSMS?
choices: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
You must DROP and recreate it
questions.correct_answer: Right-click the stored procedure > Modify — SSMS generates ALTER PROCEDURE
questions.explanation: Right-click > Modify opens a query window pre-populated with ALTER PROCEDURE.

questions.question_text: How do you save a T-SQL script in SSMS?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S saves your query to a local .sql file you can reopen later.

questions.question_text: How do you call (execute) a stored procedure with parameters in T-SQL?
questions.explanation: EXEC (or EXECUTE) followed by the procedure name and named parameters is the correct syntax.

questions.question_text: To see the actual execution plan for a query in SSMS, what do you do?
choices: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
Open a new window and type EXPLAIN
questions.correct_answer: Press Ctrl+M before running, then F5
questions.explanation: Ctrl+M toggles 'Include Actual Execution Plan' — the plan tab appears after you run the query.

questions.question_text: After writing a CREATE PROCEDURE statement in SSMS, what must you do to save it to the database?
choices: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
Both Ctrl+S and F5 are required
questions.correct_answer: Execute (F5) the CREATE PROCEDURE statement — this compiles and stores it on the server
questions.explanation: Running CREATE PROCEDURE registers it in the database. Ctrl+S only saves the script file locally.

questions.question_text: In SSMS, pressing F5 with text selected will execute only the selected text, not the entire script.
questions.explanation: If you highlight a portion of the query before pressing F5, only that portion runs.

questions.question_text: You can only have one Query Editor tab open at a time in SSMS.
questions.explanation: SSMS supports multiple tabbed Query Editor windows simultaneously.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
choices: IaaS: manage OS and above; PaaS: manage app and data only; SaaS: just use the software
