questions.correct_answer: It adds a standardized, discoverable tools/resources/prompts model that AI hosts can consume uniformly.
questions.explanation: It adds a standardized, discoverable tools/resources/prompts model that AI hosts can consume uniformly.

questions.question_text: A trade-off of adopting MCP that a solution owner should flag is:
choices: It is free of any new infrastructure
It introduces a new layer (servers, clients) to build, secure, version, and operate
questions.correct_answer: It introduces a new layer (servers, clients) to build, secure, version, and operate
questions.explanation: Standardization brings operational overhead: another layer with its own lifecycle and security needs.

questions.question_text: Match each to whether it changes state by default.

definitions: Read-only
Read-only context
Can perform an action / change state

correct_answer.An MCP tool: Can perform an action / change state

questions.explanation: Resources mirror read-only reads; tools mirror state-changing operations, useful for risk mapping.

questions.question_text: True or False: Because MCP uses the model's tool-calling under the hood, you still depend on the model choosing tools sensibly.
questions.explanation: MCP standardizes connectivity, but the host's model still decides which tools to call, so prompt/guardrail quality matters.

questions.question_text: Which is the best one-liner for 'MCP vs API' in a screening?
choices: 'APIs connect programs; MCP standardizes how AI apps discover and use tools/data, often by wrapping those very APIs'
questions.correct_answer: 'APIs connect programs; MCP standardizes how AI apps discover and use tools/data, often by wrapping those very APIs'
questions.explanation: This positions MCP as an AI-oriented standard layered over, not opposed to, traditional APIs.

questions.question_text: Fill in: Relative to bespoke function-calling glue, MCP's headline win is ___ of tool servers across many hosts.
questions.explanation: Build-once, reuse-across-hosts is MCP's core advantage over per-app wiring.

questions.question_text: When would you NOT recommend MCP? Choose the most reasonable case.
choices: A throwaway prototype with one fixed tool and no reuse or portability needs
A program that must share connectors across teams
questions.correct_answer: A throwaway prototype with one fixed tool and no reuse or portability needs
questions.explanation: Standardization overhead may not pay off for a tiny, disposable, single-tool case, an honest scoping judgment.

questions.question_text:
In two or three keywords, what does MCP reuse from existing model capabilities rather than reinventing?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: It adds a standardized, discoverable tools/resources/prompts model that AI hosts can consume uniformly.
Host, client, server are the three roles; the model lives inside the host.
Run a security/risk review, apply least privilege, add human approval and audit logging, and confirm data controls before go-live.
MCP builds on the model's existing function/tool-calling ability, standardizing the surrounding connectivity.
questions.correct_answer: MCP builds on the model's existing function/tool-calling ability, standardizing the surrounding connectivity.
questions.explanation: MCP builds on the model's existing function/tool-calling ability, standardizing the surrounding connectivity.

lessons.lesson_name: Security, Trust & Governance for Solution Owners

questions.question_text: Why are MCP tools a primary security focus for a solution owner?
choices: They can take real actions with side effects on connected systems
questions.correct_answer: They can take real actions with side effects on connected systems
questions.explanation: Action capability means a misused or malicious tool can change real systems, so tools need the tightest controls.

questions.question_text: Which principle should govern what an MCP server is allowed to do?
choices: Least privilege (only the minimum access needed)
questions.correct_answer: Least privilege (only the minimum access needed)
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits blast radius if a server, tool, or session is compromised or misused.

questions.question_text: Before a risky tool action runs, a strong control is requiring explicit ___ from the user.
questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop approval for sensitive actions is a core MCP safety practice the host should enforce.

questions.question_text: True or False: Connecting an MCP server from an untrusted third party carries supply-chain and prompt-injection risks.
questions.explanation: Untrusted servers can return malicious content or behave unexpectedly, so server provenance and trust matter.

questions.question_text: A 'prompt injection' risk via MCP means:
choices: Malicious instructions hidden in tool/resource content trick the model into unintended actions
questions.correct_answer: Malicious instructions hidden in tool/resource content trick the model into unintended actions
questions.explanation: Data returned through MCP can carry injected instructions; treat external content as untrusted input.

questions.question_text: For a remote MCP server, which control is essential that a local stdio server may not need?
questions.explanation: Network exposure demands authn/authz and TLS; a local subprocess over stdio has a smaller attack surface.

questions.question_text: Match each governance control to its purpose.

definitions: Limit each server/tool to minimum needed access
Require user confirmation before risky actions
Record what tools did for accountability
Only permit vetted, trusted servers to connect

correct_answer.Least privilege: Limit each server/tool to minimum needed access
correct_answer.Human approval gate: Require user confirmation before risky actions
correct_answer.Audit logging: Record what tools did for accountability
correct_answer.Server allow-listing: Only permit vetted, trusted servers to connect

questions.explanation: These four controls map directly to banking governance expectations: least privilege, approvals, auditability, vetting.

questions.question_text: True or False: Because MCP standardizes connections, no separate security review of each server is necessary.
questions.explanation: Standard transport does not vouch for a server's trustworthiness; each server still needs review and controls.

questions.question_text: Which control best supports accountability and incident investigation for MCP tool use?
choices: Comprehensive audit logging of tool invocations and data access
questions.correct_answer: Comprehensive audit logging of tool invocations and data access
questions.explanation: Audit trails let you reconstruct who/what acted, essential in a regulated banking environment.

questions.question_text: Fill in: The host should enforce that a user/session can only reach an ___ set of approved servers, not arbitrary ones.
questions.explanation: Allow-listing trusted servers prevents connecting to rogue or unvetted capabilities.

questions.question_text: Scenario: an assistant connected via MCP to a payments tool is asked to 'pay $50,000 now.' Best-designed behavior is:
choices: Require explicit human approval and verify authorization/limits before acting
Refuse to ever connect to payments
questions.correct_answer: Require explicit human approval and verify authorization/limits before acting
questions.explanation: High-impact actions need approval gates, authorization checks, and limits, classic banking controls applied to tools.

questions.question_text: Reverse: 'granting each MCP server only the minimum permissions it needs' is the principle of ___.
questions.explanation: Least privilege is the foundational access-control principle for MCP servers and tools.

questions.question_text: Which is a realistic data-governance concern when an MCP server exposes a banking knowledge base?
choices: Sensitive/PII data could be exposed to the model or downstream logs without proper controls
The host would lose its UI
questions.correct_answer: Sensitive/PII data could be exposed to the model or downstream logs without proper controls
questions.explanation: Data minimization, masking, and access scoping protect PII when resources/tools surface sensitive records.

questions.question_text: True or False: Treating content returned by MCP resources/tools as untrusted input is a sensible default.
questions.explanation: External content may contain injected instructions or bad data; validate and constrain how the model acts on it.

questions.question_text:
Name two governance controls a solution owner should require for a new MCP server (keywords).

Which statement best answers this?
choices: Both replace many incompatible bespoke formats with one agreed standard, enabling interoperability.
Reasonable answers include least privilege, human approval gates, audit logging, allow-listing, and authn/authz.
Run a security/risk review, apply least privilege, add human approval and audit logging, and confirm data controls before go-live.
Point-to-point/bespoke integrations multiply combinatorially; MCP collapses that to additive, reusable pieces.
questions.correct_answer: Reasonable answers include least privilege, human approval gates, audit logging, allow-listing, and authn/authz.
questions.explanation: Reasonable answers include least privilege, human approval gates, audit logging, allow-listing, and authn/authz.

questions.question_text: The 'confused deputy' style risk in MCP is best mitigated by:
choices: Scoping the server's credentials/permissions tightly and verifying the acting user's authorization
questions.correct_answer: Scoping the server's credentials/permissions tightly and verifying the acting user's authorization
questions.explanation: A server acting with its own broad rights on behalf of a less-privileged user is risky; tie actions to the real user's authorization.

questions.question_text: Fill in: For sensitive actions, designing operations to be ___ (safe to retry without duplicate effects) reduces harm from repeated tool calls.
questions.explanation: Idempotency avoids double-payments/duplicate records if a tool is invoked more than once.

questions.question_text: True or False: Server provenance (who built and maintains it) is irrelevant once it speaks MCP correctly.
questions.explanation: Protocol compliance does not equal trustworthiness; provenance, maintenance, and vetting remain critical.

questions.question_text: Which combination best reflects mature MCP governance for a regulated bank?
choices: Vet/allow-list servers + least privilege + approval gates + audit logging + data controls
Connect any server + maximum privilege + no logs
One control only: a strong password
questions.correct_answer: Vet/allow-list servers + least privilege + approval gates + audit logging + data controls
questions.explanation: Defense in depth, layering vetting, least privilege, approvals, auditability, and data protection, is the expected posture.

questions.question_text:
In keywords, what should a solution owner do before allowing an assistant to use a high-impact MCP tool in production?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: Standardization means reusable, interoperable connectors and lower lifetime integration and maintenance cost.
Run a security/risk review, apply least privilege, add human approval and audit logging, and confirm data controls before go-live.
Reasonable answers include least privilege, human approval gates, audit logging, allow-listing, and authn/authz.
Point-to-point/bespoke integrations multiply combinatorially; MCP collapses that to additive, reusable pieces.
questions.correct_answer: Run a security/risk review, apply least privilege, add human approval and audit logging, and confirm data controls before go-live.
questions.explanation: Run a security/risk review, apply least privilege, add human approval and audit logging, and confirm data controls before go-live.

questions.question_text: A balanced, non-overstated governance statement for a screening is:
choices: 'MCP is secure by default, so no controls are needed'
'MCP standardizes connectivity but shifts responsibility to owners to vet servers, enforce least privilege, gate risky actions, and log everything'
questions.correct_answer: 'MCP standardizes connectivity but shifts responsibility to owners to vet servers, enforce least privilege, gate risky actions, and log everything'
questions.explanation: MCP provides the plumbing; trust, security, and governance remain the owner's active responsibility.

questions.question_text: At an awareness level, what is A2A (Agent-to-Agent)?
choices: An open protocol that lets independent AI agents communicate and coordinate with each other
A programming language for building AI models
A cloud hosting service for running large language models
A database format for storing customer records
questions.correct_answer: An open protocol that lets independent AI agents communicate and coordinate with each other
questions.explanation: A2A is an open protocol focused on agent-to-agent communication and coordination, not a language, host, or storage format.

questions.question_text: A2A was introduced in 2025.
questions.explanation: A2A emerged in 2025 as a new open protocol; it is recent and still maturing.

questions.question_text: A2A originated at ___ and was later donated to the Linux Foundation to be governed as an open standard.
questions.explanation: A2A was Google-originated in 2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation, signaling a vendor-neutral, open direction.

questions.question_text: In one sentence, the core problem A2A is designed to solve is letting different AI ___ talk to and work with each other.
questions.explanation: A2A standardizes communication between agents so they can collaborate rather than operating in isolation.

questions.question_text: Which banking analogy best captures what A2A provides?
choices: A standard interbank messaging network (like SWIFT) that lets separate institutions exchange instructions in a common format
A single core banking system that replaces all others
An internal spreadsheet template used by one team
A printer driver installed on one workstation
questions.correct_answer: A standard interbank messaging network (like SWIFT) that lets separate institutions exchange instructions in a common format
questions.explanation: Like SWIFT lets independent banks exchange messages in a shared format, A2A lets independent agents exchange requests in a shared format.

questions.question_text: A2A is best described as a proprietary product owned and controlled by a single vendor.
questions.explanation: A2A is an open protocol; though Google-originated, it was donated to the Linux Foundation for vendor-neutral governance.

questions.question_text: The word 'protocol' in 'A2A protocol' most nearly means a:
choices: Shared set of rules and message formats that systems agree to follow so they can interoperate
Physical server where agents are stored
User interface for chatting with an AI
questions.correct_answer: Shared set of rules and message formats that systems agree to follow so they can interoperate
questions.explanation: A protocol is an agreed set of rules/formats enabling interoperability, similar to agreed messaging standards in banking.

questions.question_text: Which statement about A2A's maturity is the most accurate and honest?
choices: It is a recent (2025) and still-maturing protocol, not yet a universally adopted standard
It has been the dominant industry standard for over a decade
It is fully adopted by every major enterprise already
It is an abandoned project no longer maintained
questions.correct_answer: It is a recent (2025) and still-maturing protocol, not yet a universally adopted standard
questions.explanation: Keep expectations realistic: A2A is new in 2025 and evolving; adoption is early, not universal.

questions.question_text: True or False: A2A is mainly about a single AI agent talking to a human user through a chat box.
questions.explanation: A2A is about agents communicating with other agents, not about the human-to-agent chat interface.

questions.question_text: Match each A2A fact to its correct description.

definitions: Google
Linux Foundation
Agent-to-agent communication

questions.explanation: A2A: introduced 2025, originated at Google, donated to the Linux Foundation, purpose is agent-to-agent communication.

questions.question_text:
In your own words (keywords), what is A2A and what does it let agents do?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: They are complementary, operating at different layers: MCP for tools/data, A2A for agent collaboration.
A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
A2A promises vendor-neutral interoperability for multi-agent collaboration, reducing bespoke integrations.
A2A was introduced in 2025 and its governance was placed with the Linux Foundation.
questions.correct_answer: A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
questions.explanation: A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.

questions.question_text: A senior leader asks why A2A matters. Which one-line summary is best at an awareness level?
choices: It gives independent agents a common language so they can collaborate across vendors and teams
It makes a single agent run faster on one machine
It encrypts customer data at rest in the database
It is a new charting library for dashboards
questions.correct_answer: It gives independent agents a common language so they can collaborate across vendors and teams
questions.explanation: The value of A2A is interoperability: a shared way for agents to collaborate across organizational and vendor boundaries.

questions.question_text: A2A is intended to be vendor-neutral and open rather than locked to one provider.
questions.explanation: Donation to the Linux Foundation underscores the vendor-neutral, open intent of A2A.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: A2A is an ___ protocol, meaning its specification is openly published and not controlled by a single company.
questions.explanation: Open means the spec is public and community/foundation governed, encouraging broad adoption.

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT a goal of A2A?
choices: Replacing the need for AI models entirely
Letting agents discover and communicate with one another
Enabling interoperability across different agent providers
questions.correct_answer: Replacing the need for AI models entirely
questions.explanation: A2A is a communication layer between agents; it does not replace the underlying AI models that power those agents.

questions.question_text: True or False: Because A2A is an open standard, multiple companies can build agents that interoperate without custom one-off integrations for each pairing.
questions.explanation: A shared open protocol reduces bespoke point-to-point integrations, much like a common messaging standard does in banking.

questions.question_text: An analyst says 'A2A is just a faster AI model.' Why is this wrong?
choices: A2A is a communication protocol between agents, not a model that generates outputs
A2A is actually a slower model
A2A only works with images, not text
A2A is a type of GPU hardware
questions.correct_answer: A2A is a communication protocol between agents, not a model that generates outputs
questions.explanation: Common misconception: A2A is not a model. It is the protocol layer letting agents talk to each other.

questions.question_text:
Short answer (keywords): Name the organization that now hosts A2A governance and the year it was introduced.

Which statement best answers this?
choices: A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
A2A was introduced in 2025 and its governance was placed with the Linux Foundation.
Sensible first steps include a contained pilot/PoC, monitoring the standard, and identifying suitable use cases.
Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.
questions.correct_answer: A2A was introduced in 2025 and its governance was placed with the Linux Foundation.
questions.explanation: A2A was introduced in 2025 and its governance was placed with the Linux Foundation.

questions.question_text: The most accurate framing of A2A's relationship to existing AI tooling is that it ___ other approaches rather than replacing them.
questions.explanation: A2A is designed to complement existing approaches (such as MCP), not replace them.

questions.question_text: Which scenario is the clearest example of A2A in action?
choices: A scheduling agent and a travel-booking agent exchange messages to coordinate a trip on a customer's behalf
A user types a question into a single chatbot and reads the reply
An engineer trains a model on historical data overnight
questions.correct_answer: A scheduling agent and a travel-booking agent exchange messages to coordinate a trip on a customer's behalf
questions.explanation: A2A shines when two or more independent agents must communicate and coordinate to complete a task.

questions.question_text: True or False: At an awareness level, it is enough to describe A2A as an open, 2025 protocol for agent-to-agent communication that complements rather than replaces existing approaches.
questions.explanation: That single sentence captures the awareness essentials: open, 2025, agent-to-agent, and complementary.

questions.question_text: What is the core distinction between A2A and MCP?
choices: A2A is agents talking to other agents; MCP is an agent connecting to tools and data sources
A2A is for images; MCP is for text
A2A is closed-source; MCP is open-source
They are two names for the exact same protocol
questions.correct_answer: A2A is agents talking to other agents; MCP is an agent connecting to tools and data sources
questions.explanation: MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects an agent to tools/data; A2A connects agents to one another.

questions.question_text: True or False: A2A replaces MCP, so an enterprise should pick one and discard the other.
questions.explanation: A2A complements MCP. They address different layers and are commonly used together.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: MCP focuses on an agent using ___ and data; A2A focuses on agents coordinating with each other.
questions.explanation: MCP is the 'agent-to-tools/data' layer; A2A is the 'agent-to-agent' layer.

questions.question_text: Match each protocol to the relationship it primarily standardizes.

definitions: Agent to tools/data sources
Agent to other agents

questions.explanation: MCP = agent-to-tools/data; A2A = agent-to-agent. They sit at complementary layers.

questions.question_text: Using a banking analogy: if MCP is like giving a single analyst access to the data warehouse and reporting tools, then A2A is most like:
choices: Two analysts in different departments coordinating with each other to complete a shared deliverable
Installing a faster hard drive in the analyst's laptop
Buying a second monitor for the analyst
questions.correct_answer: Two analysts in different departments coordinating with each other to complete a shared deliverable
questions.explanation: MCP equips one agent with tools/data access; A2A is the coordination between separate agents/actors.

questions.question_text: True or False: An enterprise might use MCP and A2A together, where each agent uses tools via MCP and collaborates with other agents via A2A.
questions.explanation: The two protocols are complementary: MCP for tool/data access within an agent, A2A for cross-agent collaboration.

questions.question_text: Which statement reflects a common MISCONCEPTION you should avoid?
choices: 'A2A and MCP compete, so adopting one means rejecting the other'
'MCP connects agents to tools and data'
'A2A and MCP can be used together'
questions.correct_answer: 'A2A and MCP compete, so adopting one means rejecting the other'
questions.explanation: The competition framing is the misconception. They are complementary, addressing different needs.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: MCP stands for the ___ Context Protocol.
questions.explanation: MCP = Model Context Protocol, the standard for connecting models/agents to tools and data.

questions.question_text: An agent needs to read records from a CRM and call a calculator function. Which protocol is the natural fit?
choices: MCP, because it standardizes connecting an agent to tools and data sources
A2A, because it is for agent-to-agent messaging
Neither; this requires a brand-new protocol
Both must always be used for any single tool call
questions.correct_answer: MCP, because it standardizes connecting an agent to tools and data sources
questions.explanation: Connecting one agent to tools/data is exactly MCP's job, not A2A's.

questions.question_text: A loan-decisioning agent must hand off part of a workflow to a separate fraud-screening agent owned by another team. Which protocol fits this hand-off?
choices: A2A, because it standardizes agents communicating and coordinating with each other
MCP, because it is for connecting to a single database
Neither, because agents cannot hand off work
A2A only if both agents are from the same vendor
questions.correct_answer: A2A, because it standardizes agents communicating and coordinating with each other
questions.explanation: Cross-agent hand-off and coordination is A2A's purpose, even across teams or vendors.

questions.question_text:
Short answer (keywords): In one phrase each, what does MCP connect and what does A2A connect?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
Sensible first steps include a contained pilot/PoC, monitoring the standard, and identifying suitable use cases.
They are complementary, operating at different layers: MCP for tools/data, A2A for agent collaboration.
MCP connects an agent to tools/data; A2A connects agents to other agents.
questions.correct_answer: MCP connects an agent to tools/data; A2A connects agents to other agents.
questions.explanation: MCP connects an agent to tools/data; A2A connects agents to other agents.

questions.question_text: True or False: A2A is positioned to complement MCP, not to make it obsolete.
questions.explanation: A2A complements MCP; the two cover different interaction layers.

questions.question_text: Which layer does each protocol primarily address?

definitions: MCP
A2A

questions.explanation: MCP handles tool/data access; A2A handles inter-agent collaboration.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: A useful one-liner is 'MCP is agent-to-tools; A2A is agent-to-___.'
questions.explanation: The memorable contrast: MCP = agent-to-tools; A2A = agent-to-agent.

questions.question_text: A vendor claims 'You only need A2A; MCP is irrelevant now.' What is the best awareness-level response?
choices: They solve different problems; MCP handles tools/data access while A2A handles agent collaboration, so both can be relevant
A2A cannot work unless MCP is removed first
MCP and A2A are identical, so the claim is trivially true
questions.correct_answer: They solve different problems; MCP handles tools/data access while A2A handles agent collaboration, so both can be relevant
questions.explanation: Reject the either/or framing: the protocols are complementary and often coexist.

questions.question_text: True or False: If a single agent simply needs to query a data source, A2A is the most appropriate protocol.
questions.explanation: Querying a data source from one agent is MCP territory; A2A is for agent-to-agent communication.

questions.question_text: Which pairing correctly matches a need to its protocol?
choices: Need: an agent to call external tools -> MCP; Need: agents to delegate work to each other -> A2A
Need: an agent to call external tools -> A2A; Need: agents to delegate work to each other -> MCP
questions.correct_answer: Need: an agent to call external tools -> MCP; Need: agents to delegate work to each other -> A2A
questions.explanation: Tool calls map to MCP; inter-agent delegation maps to A2A.

questions.question_text:
Short answer (keywords): Why is it wrong to say A2A and MCP compete?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.
A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
They are complementary, operating at different layers: MCP for tools/data, A2A for agent collaboration.
MCP connects an agent to tools/data; A2A connects agents to other agents.
questions.correct_answer: They are complementary, operating at different layers: MCP for tools/data, A2A for agent collaboration.
questions.explanation: They are complementary, operating at different layers: MCP for tools/data, A2A for agent collaboration.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: When mapping a workflow, an agent reaching outward to other independent agents signals an ___ (A2A) interaction, while reaching for a database or API signals an MCP interaction.
questions.explanation: Agent-to-agent reach = A2A; agent-to-tool/data reach = MCP.

questions.question_text: True or False: A2A and MCP can be thought of as different 'lanes' that together enable richer agent ecosystems.
questions.explanation: Together MCP (tools/data) and A2A (agent collaboration) enable more capable, interoperable agent ecosystems.

questions.question_text: An agent uses MCP to fetch account data, then uses A2A to ask another agent to perform a compliance check. This shows the protocols are:
choices: Complementary, each handling a different part of the same workflow
Redundant, doing exactly the same job
In conflict, so the workflow will fail
questions.correct_answer: Complementary, each handling a different part of the same workflow
questions.explanation: This is the canonical complementary pattern: MCP for data access, A2A for delegating to another agent.

lessons.lesson_name: Core Ideas: Agent Cards, Tasks & Interoperability

questions.question_text: What is an 'Agent Card' in A2A?
choices: A published description that advertises an agent's identity and capabilities so other agents can discover it
A physical access badge for the data center
A pricing plan for an AI subscription
A credit card used to pay for compute
questions.correct_answer: A published description that advertises an agent's identity and capabilities so other agents can discover it
questions.explanation: An Agent Card describes who an agent is and what it can do, enabling discovery by other agents.

questions.question_text: True or False: In A2A, a unit of work that one agent asks another to perform is referred to as a 'Task.'
questions.explanation: A Task is the unit of work exchanged between agents in A2A.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The Agent ___ is what lets one agent discover another agent's capabilities.
questions.explanation: The Agent Card publishes capabilities for discovery, like a capabilities profile.

questions.question_text: Which banking analogy best fits an Agent Card?
choices: A service catalog entry that lists what a department offers and how to engage it
A vault combination kept secret from everyone
A monthly account statement mailed to a customer
questions.correct_answer: A service catalog entry that lists what a department offers and how to engage it
questions.explanation: An Agent Card is like a service catalog entry advertising capabilities and how to interact.

questions.question_text: Match each A2A concept to its description.

definitions: Advertises an agent's identity and capabilities
A unit of work passed between agents
Different agents working together via a shared standard

correct_answer.Agent Card: Advertises an agent's identity and capabilities
correct_answer.Task: A unit of work passed between agents
correct_answer.Interoperability: Different agents working together via a shared standard

questions.explanation: Agent Card = capability advertisement; Task = unit of work; Interoperability = collaboration via a shared standard.

questions.question_text: What does 'interoperability' mean in the A2A context?
choices: Agents built by different teams or vendors can work together because they follow the same protocol
An agent can run on any operating system
Two agents must be written in the same programming language to talk
Agents can only cooperate if they share one database
questions.correct_answer: Agents built by different teams or vendors can work together because they follow the same protocol
questions.explanation: Interoperability is the payoff of a shared standard: heterogeneous agents collaborate without bespoke integrations.

questions.question_text: True or False: Agent Cards make it possible for agents to discover each other rather than requiring every connection to be hardcoded in advance.
questions.explanation: Discovery via Agent Cards reduces the need for hardcoded, pre-arranged connections.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: In A2A, ___ is the goal of letting agents from different vendors collaborate through a common protocol.
questions.explanation: Interoperability across vendors/teams is a central aim of the A2A protocol.

questions.question_text: A requesting agent sends a Task to another agent. At an awareness level, what is a Task?
choices: A defined piece of work the receiving agent is asked to carry out and report back on
A scheduled cron job on a server
A backup of the agent's memory
questions.correct_answer: A defined piece of work the receiving agent is asked to carry out and report back on
questions.explanation: A Task is a defined piece of work delegated from one agent to another, with results returned.

questions.question_text:
Short answer (keywords): Name the A2A concept that advertises an agent's capabilities for discovery.

Which statement best answers this?
choices: The Agent Card advertises capabilities so other agents can discover and engage it.
A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.
Sensible first steps include a contained pilot/PoC, monitoring the standard, and identifying suitable use cases.
questions.correct_answer: The Agent Card advertises capabilities so other agents can discover and engage it.
questions.explanation: The Agent Card advertises capabilities so other agents can discover and engage it.

questions.question_text: Which is the clearest example of an Agent Card's purpose?
choices: A fraud-screening agent publishes what checks it can perform so a loan agent knows it can delegate screening to it
A server logs its CPU temperature every minute
An invoice is emailed to a customer
questions.correct_answer: A fraud-screening agent publishes what checks it can perform so a loan agent knows it can delegate screening to it
questions.explanation: The Agent Card advertises capabilities, enabling another agent to discover and delegate appropriately.

questions.question_text: True or False: Interoperability in A2A requires all agents to be built by the same vendor.
questions.explanation: The opposite is true: interoperability lets agents from different vendors/teams collaborate via the shared protocol.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The unit of work exchanged between A2A agents is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A Task is the delegated unit of work in A2A.

questions.question_text: Match the banking analogy to the A2A concept.

terms: A work ticket handed to another team
definitions: Agent Card
Task
Interoperability

questions.explanation: Agent Card ~ service catalog entry; Task ~ work ticket; Interoperability ~ a shared standard enabling collaboration.

questions.question_text: Why are Agent Cards important for a multi-agent ecosystem?
choices: They enable discovery, so agents can find and understand each other's capabilities without prior hardcoding
They store the agent's billing information
They encrypt all network traffic by default
They are required to train the underlying model
questions.correct_answer: They enable discovery, so agents can find and understand each other's capabilities without prior hardcoding
questions.explanation: Discovery is the key benefit: Agent Cards let agents learn what others can do.

questions.question_text: True or False: A Task in A2A can include the request and, when completed, a result returned to the requesting agent.
questions.explanation: A Task captures the requested work and carries back results upon completion, at an awareness level.

questions.question_text:
Short answer (keywords): What is the benefit of interoperability in A2A for an enterprise?

Which statement best answers this?
choices: A solid awareness answer: A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents communicate and coordinate/interoperate.
Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.
The Agent Card advertises capabilities so other agents can discover and engage it.
A2A was introduced in 2025 and its governance was placed with the Linux Foundation.
questions.correct_answer: Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.
questions.explanation: Interoperability lets heterogeneous agents collaborate via a shared standard, reducing bespoke integrations.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: An Agent Card primarily supports the process of ___, where one agent finds another whose capabilities match a need.
questions.explanation: Agent Cards power discovery of suitable agents based on advertised capabilities.

questions.question_text: Which trio lists three core A2A ideas?
questions.explanation: The awareness-level trio: Agent Cards (discovery), Tasks (units of work), and Interoperability (collaboration via a shared standard).

questions.question_text: True or False: Without a shared protocol like A2A, connecting agents from different vendors typically means more custom, one-off integrations.
questions.explanation: A shared protocol reduces bespoke point-to-point work, which is the value of interoperability.

questions.question_text: A loan agent reads a fraud-screening agent's Agent Card, then sends it a Task; both follow the A2A spec. Which concepts are illustrated?
choices: Agent Card (discovery), Task (unit of work), and Interoperability (shared protocol)
questions.correct_answer: Agent Card (discovery), Task (unit of work), and Interoperability (shared protocol)
questions.explanation: This single scenario showcases all three core ideas working together.

lessons.lesson_name: Where A2A Fits in an Enterprise Roadmap

questions.question_text: At an awareness level, where does A2A fit on an enterprise AI roadmap?
choices: As an emerging interoperability layer to watch and pilot as multi-agent use cases mature
As a fully proven core system to rip-and-replace everything immediately
As a replacement for the enterprise data warehouse
As a consumer mobile app feature
